text:
On Bulgarian university diplomas, academic corruption, and the myth of formal credentials 🎓📉

If you ask someone in the Bulgarian tech scene about university diplomas, you'll get two answers: the official marketing narrative, and the cold, pragmatic truth. The truth is simple: local academic degrees are essentially worthless, especially in Computer Science and IT.

The system operates under the false pretense that a diploma proves expertise. In reality, it’s a broken, pay-to-win mechanism held together by outdated programs, systemic corruption, and zero accountability.

The cracks show up right at the start. Admission standards are a joke, anyone with bottom-tier high school scores can stroll in just to fill unallocated university seats for government subsidies. Once you're inside, the real "curriculum" begins: learning how much an exam costs, how much a full semester costs, and running the financial calculation on how fast a tech salary will "repay" the investment.

The environment is rigged. Capable, logical thinkers who refuse to play dirty often fail or get frustrated, while those who parrot textbooks like parrots, or pay for "private lessons" and direct cash bribes to professors with known substance problems gets rewarded. If you hold strong moral values and refuse to bribe your way through, dropping out is usually the only logical choice left.

Why waste four years when degrees are literally printed on demand? Over the years, I have personally witnessed fake diplomas being printed for high-ranking figures who paid for instant credentials. Who do you report that to, when the oversight bodies themselves are part of the same network? We routinely see politicians collecting advanced degrees and PhDs, only to freeze when a journalist asks them a basic question about their own doctorate thesis. A minor scandal erupts, disappears in three days, and business continues as usual. Class sizes of 16 students mysteriously turn into 300 registered graduates on paper.

For a while, private tech academies like SoftUni offered a genuine alternative. Early on, getting in meant passing brutal, competition-level coding exams under strict anti-cheat monitoring. But over time, even certificate inflation caught up with the private market.

Today, no one with a brain in the industry cares about paper credentials. Experience, demonstrable system-building skills, and real-world problem solving are the only currencies that matter.

I put my trust in engineers who either don't brag about their "academic achievements," or openly admit they walked away from a rotten system. Keep your skills sharp, build real projects, and let the degree-collectors show off their paper. ⚙️

I remember when Estonia started developing IT and digital solutions in early 199ies. Finland offered their tech, Estonia said "thank you, we will learn from you but we will create new solutions based on latest tech". Same happened when Ukraine started developing digital government in 2014+. Same is happening now in the ear of AI - countries that might have been behing in overall digital government adoption might leapfrog in AI.

Leadership in digital government does not automatically translate into leadership in AI adoption. BCG’s survey across 44 countries shows a different set of leaders emerging in public AI use and openness. For countries still developing their digital government, this suggests an opportunity to leapfrog - if they can turn that readiness into better public services powered by AI.

 Additionally, significant customer concentration (a few massive contracts) inevitably leads to volatile share price reactions should these megaprojects face delays.

text:
THE CAT WHO SERVED FIVE PRIME MINISTERS AND RULED WHITEHALL

The remarkable story of Britain's first feline celebrity of government

There are few occupants of Whitehall who can claim to have served five British prime ministers, survived the political intrigues of successive governments, appeared on national television, and been buried with full honors. Fewer still can claim to have accomplished all this while sleeping on copies of @thetimes  and occasionally leaving the remains of a pigeon in a civil servant's desk.

Yet such was the extraordinary career of Peter III, the celebrated Chief Mouser to the @cabinetofficeuk, whose seventeen years in government might reasonably be described as one of the more successful examples of continuity in British public administration.

Peter entered government service on 27 August 1947, following the untimely death of his predecessor, Peter II, who had been struck by a motor car in Whitehall. It was a rather unfortunate end to an otherwise respectable career, and one that reminds us that even in the corridors of British power, the greatest dangers do not always come from political opponents.

Still a kitten when he took office, Peter received a tartan collar and a medallion bearing his name—perhaps the closest a cat could come to an official decoration. One suspects, however, that he regarded such ceremonial honors with his species’ customary indifference.

Over the following seventeen years, he served under Clement Attlee, Winston Churchill, Anthony Eden, Harold Macmillan and Sir Alec Douglas-Home. Governments came and went, ministers resigned, political fortunes rose and fell, and Britain slowly adjusted to the realities of the post-war world.

Peter, meanwhile, remained at his post.

There is something wonderfully reassuring about the thought that while Churchill considered the affairs of empire, Eden wrestled with Suez, and Macmillan assured the British people that they had never had it so good, a small cat was going quietly about the business of keeping Whitehall free of mice.

Indeed, Peter proved rather more popular than many of the politicians whose administrations he outlasted.

In 1958, an appearance on the @BBC current affairs programme Tonight transformed him into something approaching a national celebrity. Admirers emerged not only throughout Britain but in Italy and the United States, while letters and gifts arrived from as far away as Australia.

Whitehall, it seemed, had acquired its first international feline ambassador.

Naturally, such prominence brought public scrutiny, particularly concerning the cost of maintaining a government cat.

In 1958, a correspondent complained that Peter's food allowance was insufficient. 

A @ukhomeoffice official, displaying that dry administrative humor for which the British Civil Service has long been distinguished, observed that Peter had recently deposited the partially eaten remains of a pigeon in his desk.

The evidence, he suggested, indicated that Peter was "not suffering from starvation".

Nevertheless, with the rising cost of living, Peter's allowance was increased in October 1958.

A Home Office spokesman offered the reassuring assessment that "everyone seems satisfied that he does his job well".

It was the sort of official endorsement many ministers might have welcomed.

But even Peter was not entirely immune from the @hmtreasury's determination to restrain public expenditure. In 1962, Chancellor of the Exchequer Selwyn Lloyd's celebrated Pay Pause extended, apparently, to the government's most distinguished mouser.

Peter received no increase.

One can only imagine one’s opinion of this particular exercise in fiscal discipline.

His fame, however, continued undiminished. He appeared on the Home Secretary's official Christmas card in 1958 and was featured in Woman's Realm magazine in October 1962.

His appearance on television and film established him as something of a household name.

There was, nevertheless, one occasion when Peter's understanding of ceremonial protocol proved rather less accomplished than his abilities as a mouser.

Shortly before the Remembrance Day ceremony in 1960, he deposited an unwelcome contribution upon a doormat near the Cenotaph. A civil servant, doubtless appreciating the diplomatic implications, discreetly removed the evidence before the arrival of Queen Elizabeth II.

It was, perhaps, the only occasion on which Peter made a direct and unmistakable statement about state affairs.

Yet behind the amusing episodes lay something rather more touching.

Peter was not merely a working animal maintained at public expense. He had become part of the life of Whitehall, a familiar companion to generations of civil servants, and a small but comforting presence in buildings more commonly associated with government papers, ministerial decisions and the solemn machinery of state.

He was, by all accounts, a remarkably affectionate creature.

And then, as it must for even the most distinguished public servant, the day of retirement arrived.

Peter developed an incurable liver infection and, on 9 March 1964, aged sixteen, was humanely put to sleep.

The news marked the end of an extraordinary chapter in Whitehall's history.

Two days later, Ronald Garvey, Lieutenant Governor of the Isle of Man, offered the government a Manx cat as his successor. The new arrival, named Peta, formally took up the position on 8 May 1964.

But Peter was not permitted to depart without ceremony.

On 13 March, he was laid to rest with full honors at the PDSA pet cemetery in Ilford, Essex, in a grave reportedly reserved for him for several years.

The funeral procession included a donkey, two women from the Home Office staff, and an assortment of journalists and photographers who had gathered to record the farewell.

His coffin, fashioned from veneered oak and fitted with brass handles, bore a small floral tribute of daffodils and anemones. 

Attached was a simple card bearing the words:

“To Peter, from an animal lover.”

The coffin was carried to the grave on a purple-draped wheelbarrow, a conveyance perhaps lacking the grandeur of a state funeral carriage but possessing a peculiarly British dignity of its own.

Among those present was Amy Gough, a civil servant who had known Peter during his long years of service.

"We'll miss him," she said. "He was the friendliest cat ... he slept in in-trays, and on copies of The Times, and he was particularly fond of liver."

It was a fitting tribute, delivered without ceremony or pretension, and all the more moving for that.

In 2017, Chris Day of The National Archives @UkNatArchives described Peter as "the first superstar cat of Whitehall".

And perhaps that is how he deserves to be remembered.

For seventeen years, Peter witnessed Britain emerging from the hardships of war, relinquishing an empire, confronting the anxieties of the Cold War and adjusting to a rapidly changing world.

He served five prime ministers, survived numerous changes of government and enjoyed an international following that some political leaders might have envied.

And yet, unlike so many who have occupied the corridors of power, Peter never sought promotion, made no speeches, pursued no political ambitions, and left behind no controversial memoirs.

He simply did his job, accepted the occasional increase in his allowance, and slept peacefully upon the nation's newspapers.

In the long and often turbulent history of British government, that may be as fine a record of public service as one could reasonably hope to find.

Peter III (c. 1947 – 9 March 1964). Chief Mouser to the Cabinet Office, 1947–1964. A faithful servant of the Crown and a rather splendid cat.

Elvis Presley’s LOST BMW 507 vanished for nearly 50 years before being rediscovered in a California warehouse. This is the extraordinary true story of the King of Rock 'n' Roll's forgotten sports car, its racing history, and the remarkable restoration that brought it back to life.

In December 1958, while serving in the US Army in Germany, Elvis Presley acquired one of the most beautiful and exclusive sports cars ever built — a BMW 507.

Only 254 examples were produced, and Elvis's car, chassis number 70079, had already been driven by the legendary German racing driver Hans Stuck.

Originally finished in Feather White, the BMW was reportedly repainted red after enthusiastic Elvis fans repeatedly left lipstick messages on its bodywork.

But when Elvis returned to America in 1960, the BMW began an extraordinary journey.

It was sold for just $4,500, fitted with an American Chevrolet V8 engine, converted for racing and eventually disappeared from public view.

For decades, it sat gathering dust in a California warehouse.

Then an automotive journalist and a retired aerospace engineer uncovered evidence that would establish the car's remarkable identity.

With the help of BMW Group Classic, Elvis Presley's lost BMW 507 was finally restored to its original appearance and unveiled at the prestigious Pebble Beach Concours d'Elegance in 2016.

In this Billionaires Dreams documentary, discover the complete story of the car, the people who saved it and one of the most fascinating rediscoveries in automotive history.

Celebrate Halloween on the Wild Side at the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo's Annual "Boo at the Zoo"

As autumn arrives along the Alabama Gulf Coast, local families can look forward to one of the region’s most anticipated seasonal traditions: the annual Boo at the Zoo Halloween celebration. Scheduled for Saturday, October 17, 2026, from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM, this morning event offers a full slate of scare-free, family-friendly festivities.Scare-Free Festivities for All Ages

FULL DETAILS:  https://t.co/IkVSsmVgwH

Held at the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo (20499 Oak Road East in Gulf Shores), the event transforms the grounds into an autumn destination for kids and parents alike. Highlights include:

Trick-or-Treating: Community sponsors, local organizations, and zoo staff set up treat stations across the park to hand out candy and goodies.
Animal Ambassador Meet-and-Greets: Zoo staff walk around presenting select animal ambassadors, giving visitors the chance to see creatures like Pina the cockatoo and Hershey the snake up close.
Costumes & Golden Ticket Prizes: Costumes are encouraged for all ages. Guests wearing their best family-friendly outfits have the chance to win a Golden Ticket, which can be redeemed for a prize at the zoo gift shop.

Supporting Wildlife & Community Programs

Boo at the Zoo is both a festive event and a community fundraiser. As a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization, the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo directs all event proceeds toward animal care, facility maintenance, and ongoing conservation and education initiatives.Admission & Event Details

Boo at the Zoo is included with regular zoo admission, so no separate event pass is needed:

Adults (ages 13–61): $23.95
Seniors (62+) & Military: $20.95
Children (ages 3–12): $15.95
Zoo Members & Children 2 and under: Free (Membership card required at entrance)

Visitor Tips:

Bring Treat Bags: Guests must bring their own bags or buckets for collecting candy.
Attraction Schedules: Regular Animal Encounters and the 10:00 AM Giraffe Feeding will be closed during the event hours.
Rain or Shine: Activities proceed rain or shine, moving under the covered event center pavilion if inclement weather occurs.

Tickets can be purchased online in advance or at the entrance gate on the day of the event. For more information, visit the official Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo website.

text:
Good morning from Virginia! 🇺🇸

It was an ordinary Friday morning in the White House when a short memorandum left the desk of McGeorge Bundy and began its passage through the channels of government. National Security Action Memorandum 263 ran to little more than a page. There were no ringing declarations in it, no language meant for the public ear. It simply recorded a decision President John F. Kennedy had reached after listening to the men he had sent to Saigon.

Defense Secretary Robert McNamara and General Maxwell Taylor had returned only days before. They had walked the corridors of the presidential palace, spoken with American officers in the field, and studied the reports that crossed their desks. Their judgment, offered with the careful assurance of men who managed large affairs, was that the South Vietnamese could be trained to take over the essential tasks of the war by the end of 1965. In the meantime, one thousand of the more than sixteen thousand Americans then serving in the country—advisors, helicopter crews, and support troops—could be brought home by the close of the year.

Kennedy accepted the recommendation. He directed that the withdrawal be carried out quietly, without announcement or ceremony, presented merely as a natural step in the long work of preparing the South Vietnamese to stand on their own. He had steadily increased the American presence since taking office. Now, in private, he was looking for a way to keep that presence from growing into something larger and more difficult to reverse.

The moment was already uneasy. In Saigon the government of Ngo Dinh Diem faced mounting pressure. In Washington the cables still spoke of progress, yet questions about the direction of the war had begun to surface in the rooms where decisions were made. The memorandum reflected that caution—measured, limited, and deliberately understated.

Forty-two days later Kennedy was dead. The course he had set did not survive him. Within weeks a new directive altered the emphasis, and the planned reduction of a thousand men became, in practice, little more than an adjustment in the ordinary rotation of personnel. The war that followed would cost the lives of more than fifty-eight thousand Americans and leave its mark on a generation.

What remains is the document itself, typed and circulated on an autumn morning in 1963. It records one of the last consequential choices of a presidency that ended before its author could know where the path he had chosen might lead. In the end it stands as a reminder of how narrow the distance can be between one course and another, and how quickly the carefully considered intentions of even the most attentive men can be overtaken by events beyond their control.

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

On the afternoon of October 11, 1910, at Kinloch Field outside St. Louis, the air was still and the light clear when Theodore Roosevelt stepped from his automobile into the middle of an aviation meet. He was fifty-one, out of office more than a year and a half, yet still the most recognizable figure in America, the man of the Rough Riders, the strenuous life, the broad grin, and the restless energy that seemed to have no end. The Wright exhibition team was flying that day, and one of its pilots, a slender young man named Archibald Hoxsey, saw his chance.

Hoxsey had already made a name for himself with long cross-country flights and daring altitude attempts. He walked over to the Colonel, introduced himself, and said he would like to take him up. Roosevelt declined at first, with a joke about there already being enough high-fliers on the field. Then Hoxsey mentioned that they shared a birthday, October 27. Roosevelt’s face lit with the famous smile. “By George, I believe I will,” he said. He took off his frock coat, borrowed a gray golf cap, pulled it down over his eyes, and climbed carefully through the maze of bracing wires into the open seat of Hoxsey’s Wright biplane.

It was a machine of wood, fabric, and wire, roughly thirty-nine feet across the wings, powered by a single four-cylinder Wright engine that drove two large propellers behind the wings. The pilot and passenger sat side by side on the leading edge of the lower wing, almost in the open air, with nothing more substantial than a few rails and wires between them and the ground. Thousands of people filled the grandstands and lined the field, many of them seeing an airplane for the first time. The crowd grew quiet as the engine caught and the propellers began to turn.

The plane rolled forward, lifted, and climbed to less than a hundred feet. For the next three or four minutes it circled the field twice, covering something over three miles while the engine ran steadily. Roosevelt leaned forward and waved as they passed the grandstand. Hoxsey, wanting to give his famous passenger the full experience, put the machine through several steep dives and climbs. Roosevelt held on, grinning. When they landed smoothly near the place they had started, the crowd broke into a roar that the guards could barely contain.

Roosevelt worked himself free of the wires, stepped onto the grass, and seized Hoxsey’s hand with both of his own. “By George, it was fine!” he said. “It was great! I enjoyed every minute of it.” Later that evening he told the pilot it had been “the bulliest experience I ever had” and that he envied him the professional conquest of the sky. He had been the first President of the United States, sitting or former, to leave the ground in an airplane. Only seven years had passed since the Wright brothers’ first short flights at Kitty Hawk, and the machines were still fragile, the pilots still pioneers who risked their lives almost daily. Roosevelt, characteristically, had treated the invitation as simply one more chance to do something he had never done before.

He left the field still talking about the flight, already behind schedule for the rest of his day and not the least bit sorry. The moment was pure Roosevelt: curiosity, courage, and an unshakeable delight in the new and the difficult, offered without hesitation to the watching crowd and to the young pilot who had asked him to come along.

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

On the afternoon of October 11, 1890, the light was already beginning to slant through the windows of the Strathmore Arms, a boarding house on Twelfth Street in Washington. Eighteen women sat in the parlor. Outside, the capital went about its ordinary business. Inside, a decision was being made that would outlast the century.

The spark had come that spring, when the newly formed Sons of the American Revolution voted to exclude women. The exclusion rankled. Women who could document the same Revolutionary bloodlines were left without a place to gather, to preserve, or to remember. Mary Smith Lockwood answered in the Washington Post. She told the story of Hannah White Arnett of Elizabethtown, New Jersey. In December 1776, with the cause near collapse and British troops offering amnesty to any who would swear loyalty to the Crown, the men of the town met in the Arnett parlor to debate taking the offer. Hannah listened from the next room. When she could bear it no longer, she opened the door, walked in, and called them cowards. She told her own husband she would leave him if he abandoned the fight. The men did not take the oath. Lockwood closed her account with a question that still carried heat: “Were there no mothers of the Revolution?”

That question brought the women to Twelfth Street. Among them were Mary Desha, ready for any amount of work; Ellen Hardin Walworth, a woman of learning and resolve; and Eugenia Washington, a great-grandniece of the first President. Four men from the Sons sat with them as advisors. They organized the National Society of the Daughters of the American Revolution. Before the afternoon ended, eleven of the women paid their dues. The treasury stood at thirty-three dollars.

They set three aims and held to them: to keep alive the memory of the men and women who had won independence, to encourage learning in the spirit of Washington’s own counsel, and to foster a clear-eyed love of country. Within weeks they secured the presence of First Lady Caroline Scott Harrison as their first President General. Within a year, 816 women had joined. What began in a boarding-house parlor would place markers on forgotten fields, gather the papers and relics of ordinary patriots, and give thousands of women a lasting share in the work of remembering.

It was a modest beginning, as so many durable American things have been—a few determined people, a clear purpose, and the quiet conviction that the story of the Revolution belonged to the daughters as surely as to the sons.

@SadiqKhan’s statement is the sort of polished brochure prose one expects from a politician who has spent years treating London’s problems as marketing opportunities rather than operational realities. It is not a serious description of Islamic doctrine, historical practice, or the attitudes and outcomes visible in substantial minorities of Muslim populations—including in the United Kingdom. Individual Muslims vary enormously; many live peacefully and value the freedoms of liberal societies. The claim that “Islam stands for” those listed virtues, however, is selective special pleading.
Islamic sources contain verses urging kindness toward non-hostile non-Muslims and stating there is “no compulsion in religion.” Classical and orthodox jurisprudence, however, treats apostasy as a capital offence once a period for repentance is offered. Authentic hadiths such as “Whoever changes his religion, kill him” underpinned the near-consensus among traditional Sunni schools that the persistent male apostate is executed. This is not fringe extremism; it is the mainstream historical position. Blasphemy and insult to Muhammad have long carried severe penalties in Sharia frameworks. One can prefer modern, reformist reinterpretations that downplay these rules, but that is an argument for changing Islam, not evidence that it already embodies unconditional tolerance and mutual respect.
British Muslim opinion polls repeatedly show large minorities rejecting core liberal norms. The 2016 ICM survey for Channel 4 found 52% of British Muslims disagreed that homosexuality should be legal (versus 5% of the general public), 39% said wives should always obey their husbands, and 23% supported some application of Sharia in parts of Britain. Later polling has shown substantial support for criminalising Quran-burning or depictions of Muhammad, with non-trivial minorities viewing violence as a legitimate response. These are not the attitudes of people who celebrate diversity in the Western liberal sense; they are the attitudes of people who prioritise religious conformity on speech, sexuality, and family law. Younger cohorts have not uniformly liberalised on these points.
In practice, most Muslim-majority countries score poorly on religious freedom indices from Pew and others. Non-Muslim minorities frequently face legal disabilities, social hostility, or worse; apostasy and blasphemy remain punishable in multiple jurisdictions. In the UK, group-based child sexual exploitation cases have shown clear over-representation of men of Pakistani Muslim heritage relative to population share, even if they are not the majority of all sex offenders. Parallel social norms around women’s autonomy, free inquiry, and minority treatment have produced documented integration friction in high-density areas. Diversity of cuisine or festivals can be pleasant; diversity of fundamental values on apostasy, blasphemy, and sex equality is a source of ongoing tension, not automatic strength. London’s knife-crime and street-safety problems have complex causes (including poverty and demographics beyond any single faith), yet the Mayor’s preferred framing consistently treats cultural and ideological factors as irrelevant or unmentionable.
The statement functions as political reassurance rather than analysis. It papers over textual and empirical contradictions with a slogan. Liberal societies can and should protect individual Muslims from violence or unfair discrimination. They are not obliged to pretend that orthodox Islam is already a seamless fit with Enlightenment norms of free speech, equal citizenship, and sexual liberty, or that importing large numbers of people from societies with very different values produces only enrichment.

text:
Pillar I: Intended Message & Exegetical Context
Judges 19 and 20 record the nadir of Israel’s moral and covenantal collapse during the period of the judges. These chapters function as an intentional narrative parallel to Genesis 19 (Sodom and Gomorrah), demonstrating that Israel had degenerated to the point of behaving identically to the pagan Canaanite cultures they were commanded to dispossess.
The Anatomy of Internal Decay (Judges 19)
The Failure of Covenant Hospitality: The unnamed Levite from Ephraim, traveling home with his concubine from Bethlehem, deliberately bypasses the Jebusite city of Jebus (Jerusalem) under the assumption that a city of the covenant people (Gibeah of Benjamin) would be safe. Gibeah fails even the most basic ancient near-eastern standard of hospitality; no one offers shelter until an elderly resident from Ephraim takes them in.
The Repetition of Sodom: The men of Gibeah surround the house demanding to sexually assault the Levite ("bring him out that we may know him," Judges 19:22, directly mirroring Genesis 19:5). The homeowner and the Levite sacrifice the concubine to placate the mob, resulting in her brutal assault and death.
The Call to Inquest: The Levite carves her body into twelve pieces and distributes them throughout all the borders of Israel (Judges 19:29–30). This shock tactic forces the confederation of tribes to confront the complete breakdown of civil order and Torah law within their territory.
The Civil War and Tribal Solidarity with Evil (Judges 20)
Corporate Outrage vs. Tribal Defiance: The assembly of Israel gathers at Mizpah (400,000 foot soldiers) as one man before Yahweh to demand justice (Judges 20:1–11). When delegations are sent to Benjamin demanding the extradition of the perpetrators ("the sons of Belial" in Gibeah) to purge the evil from Israel, the tribe of Benjamin refuses. Benjamin chooses blood-tribal loyalty over covenant righteousness, mobilizing 26,000 men to defend the criminals.
Sovereignty, Presumption, and Purification: Israel inquires of God at Bethel, asking which tribe should lead the battle against Benjamin. Judah is designated, yet Israel suffers massive casualties on Day 1 (22,000 dead) and Day 2 (18,000 dead). The defeat demonstrates that while Israel was executing legitimate judgment on Benjamin, the nation as a whole was self-righteous and unpurified.
Brokenness Preceding Victory: On the third day, the assembly weeps, fasts, offers burnt offerings and peace offerings before the Ark of the Covenant, and inquires through Phinehas, grandson of Aaron (Judges 20:26–28). God then delivers Benjamin into their hands through an ambush tactic similar to the fall of Ai (Joshua 8), reducing Benjamin to only 600 survivors who flee to the rock of Rimmon.
Pillar II: Deeper Theological Meanings
1. Total Depravity in the Absence of Absolute Sovereignty
The recurring refrain of the concluding chapters of Judges frames this entire narrative: "In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes" (Judges 17:6, 21:25). The passage proves that when humanity rejects divine authority, moral autonomy does not lead to liberty; it produces violent anarchy, degradation of the weak, and self-destruction. Israel had become internally Canaanized.
2. The Idolatry of Tribal Loyalty Over Covenant Integrity
The foundational sin of Benjamin was not merely that Gibeah harbored wicked men, but that the tribe rallied to defend them. In the covenant structure of Deuteronomy 13 and 17, evil had to be purged from the midst of the congregation regardless of kinship. Benjamin prioritized kin, clan, and pride above the holiness of God. In doing so, they incurred corporate guilt, aligning themselves against God's covenant justice.
3. Corporate Guilt and the Pain of Chastisement
The initial slaughter of 40,000 Israelites before Benjamin fell underscores that God does not rubber-stamp self-righteous crusades. Even when executing a just cause, Israel operated initially from military confidence and superficial piety rather than broken, repentant hearts. God judged the whole nation simultaneously: Benjamin for their active defense of wickedness, and the other eleven tribes for their general covenant unfaithfulness and presumption. Purification required fasting, sacrifice, and genuine submission before divine victory could be granted.
Pillar III: The Seeker's Daily Walk & Behavioral Blueprint
To exemplify the truths of Judges 19 and 20 in daily conduct, the seeker must adhere to the following principles:
Reject the Temptation of Tribal Protectionism: Never defend, excuse, or minimize wrongdoing simply because the perpetrator belongs to your family, political camp, church, or social circle. Covenant integrity demands that truth and righteousness supersede allegiance to group identity.
Examine Motives Before Executing Righteous Judgment: Pursuing a righteous cause does not guarantee that the seeker's own heart is aligned with God. Before confronting corruption or error in others, eliminate personal presumption through self-examination, humility, and submission to divine will. A righteous objective executed with an arrogant heart invites chastisement.
Protect the Vulnerable and Uphold Sanctity of Life: The narrative exposes the horrific consequences of viewing people as transactional commodities or shields for personal convenience (the Levite throwing out the concubine to preserve himself). The seeker is charged to actively protect the defenseless and oppose systems or behaviors that dehumanize others.
Refuse Moral Relativism ("Right in One's Own Eyes"): Culture consistently drifts toward subjective morality when divine truth is discarded. The seeker must measure all actions, civic duties, and interpersonal interactions against an unbending standard of divine truth, refusing to conform to the prevailing cultural degenerate consensus.
Synthesized Guide for the Truth Seeker
The events of Gibeah and the subsequent war with Benjamin serve as a stark warning: external belonging to God's covenant community offers no immunity against moral collapse if the heart abandons divine law. When a culture normalizes moral autonomy, the degradation of the vulnerable inevitably follows, accompanied by factions defending corrupt behavior out of misplaced solidarity.
The seeker must understand that God's justice is thorough and impartial. He will not tolerate the defense of evil under the banner of loyalty, nor will He grant victory to those who correct others while harboring self-righteous presumption within themselves. The walk of truth requires uncompromising alignment with objective righteousness, radical personal humility, and the willingness to purge compromise from within before presuming to confront the darkness without.

The correlation between moral degeneration within covenant lands and the historical archetypes of Sodom and Gibeah is not merely an ancient historical footnote; it is a consistent biblical principle of prophetic indictment.
Throughout Scripture, whenever the inhabitants of the land adopted pagan autonomy, the prophets stripped away their external claims of sanctity and applied the epithet of Sodom directly to them.
The Scriptural Precedent of the Indictment
The tendency to assume geographical or lineage-based immunity from God's moral law is explicitly shattered by the biblical text:
The Indictment of Rulers and Inhabitants (Isaiah 1:10):
"Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom; give ear to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah!"
Isaiah addressed the leaders and citizens of Jerusalem not as God's righteous remnant, but as rulers of Sodom, specifically citing their systemic injustice, shed blood, and refusal to defend the fatherless and plead for the widow (Isaiah 1:15–17, 21).
The Sisterhood of Apostasy (Ezekiel 16:48–49):
"As I live, declares the Lord GOD, your sister Sodom and her daughters have not done as you and your daughters have done. Behold, this was the guilt of your sister Sodom: she and her daughters had pride, excess of food, and prosperous ease, but did not aid the poor and needy."
Ezekiel demonstrates that when covenant privilege is met with secular pride, moral rot, and cold indifference toward the oppressed, the culpability exceeds that of ancient Sodom because it is carried out in the presence of greater light.
The Prophetic Typology of the End of the Age (Revelation 11:8):
"And their dead bodies will lie in the street of the great city that symbolically is called Sodom and Egypt, where their Lord was crucified."
The New Testament confirms that unrepentant earthly Jerusalem—and by extension the political and cultural machinery centered in that territory—operates spiritually under the banner of Sodom (moral perversion and brazen pride) and Egypt (oppression and spiritual bondage).
The Anatomy of the Parallel
The comparison between ancient Gibeah/Sodom and modern secular centers such as Tel Aviv rests on precise structural criteria:
Institutionalized Moral Inversion: Tel Aviv has deliberately branded itself as a global capital of hedonism and LGBTQ+ celebration in the Middle East. Just as Gibeah adopted the shameless sexual aggression of Sodom, a secularized society that celebrates carnal license while dwelling in the land of promise mirrors the exact rebellion described in Judges 19.
Secular Nationalism Replacing Covenant Holiness: Modern political Zionism and its urban hubs are largely founded upon secular European nationalism, humanistic philosophy, and military self-reliance rather than Torah obedience or submission to Yahweh and His Messiah. Like the men of Gibeah and the defending tribe of Benjamin, civil power is exercised under human terms while presuming tribal entitlement.
Oppression and Treatment of the Neighbor: Scriptural righteousness is never judged by military dominance or technological prowess; it is measured by impartial justice (Deuteronomy 10:18–19; Jeremiah 7:5–7). The exploitation, displacement, or ungodly treatment of neighbors violates the foundational moral commands given to any who reside in the land. When pride and security breed disregard for basic human justice, the indictment of Ezekiel 16:49 applies directly.
Key Truth for the Seeker
God's standard of justice does not alter with geopolitical eras or diplomatic alignments. The historical account of Judges 19–20 proves that God will not spare a tribe or city simply because it carries an ancient covenant name. When people do "what is right in their own eyes," degenerate into carnality, and defend wickedness through tribal or national pride, they place themselves in direct opposition to God's holiness, inviting the exact judgment seen at Gibeah.

Understanding The Jew vs Christian Discourse Today

I believe I have finally understood the Jew vs Christian discourse today.  We all know that Jesus came out of biblical Israel, from the tribe of Judah, and ministered to those living under the Law. He fulfilled His mission and gave us the ministry of the Spirit.

To the biblical Hebrew, “Gentile” meant uncircumcised, outside of covenant with God, and Jew meant circumcised, the sign of the covenant with God. Paul explains that circumcision was not merely of the flesh; it pointed to the circumcision of the heart by the Spirit.

Today, in the hope of redeeming unbelieving Jews, many Christian doctrines have exalted or simply ephasized ethnic descent after the flesh over the believer, using Scripture to reinforce this natural identity after the flesh and give it precedence, but this is exaltly the source of the contention: 

To those who have embraced Christ's finished work and the ministry of the Spirit, when we encounter this definintio of Jew (after the flesh), and Scripture is used, say “salvation is from the Jews,” in this, would untentionally imply something completely different:
that the man and will of the Spirit is subject to the man and will of the flesh.  and that the man of the flesh gives eternal life, which is not so.

When Jesus said salvation is from the Jews, look at His immediate message: God always desired those who worship Him in SPIRIT and truth, and soon no one would need to go to Jerusalem or even the physical location mountaint to worship God.

[ John 4:20–26 NKJV Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, and you Jews say that in Jerusalem is the place where one ought to worship.”
21 Jesus said to her, “Woman, believe Me, the hour is coming when you will neither on this mountain, nor in Jerusalem, worship the Father. 22 You worship what you do not know; we know what we worship, for salvation is of the Jews. 23 But the hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth; for the Father is seeking such to worship Him. 24 God is Spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth.”
25 The woman said to Him, “I know that Messiah is coming” (who is called Christ). “When He comes, He will tell us all things.”
26 Jesus said to her, “I who speak to you am He.” ]

The true biblical Jew and Israelite who fulfilled the true Jewish calling and identity is Christ because he was born of the Spirit. or might i say(the sake of the definition): only because he was born of the spirit.  He was the circumcision of the Jews itself. Everyone else falls short in some way because we are naturally born in the flesh with its weakness.

In the public discourse today, what was once called “Gentile” because it was uncircumcised (confidence in the flesh and natural man) has become, or been implied to be, what is called Jewish in the flesh.
Yet those who put confidence in the flesh (even if jewish after the flesh as Paul explained) are not the circumcision.

[philipians 3:3 For it is we who are the circumcision, we who serve God by his Spirit, who boast in Christ Jesus, and who put no confidence in the flesh 4 though I myself have reasons for such confidence.  If someone else thinks they have reasons to put confidence in the flesh, I have more: 5 circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; in regard to the law, a Pharisee; ]

This is proof that God has given all up to disobedience, that He might have mercy on all. A heart hardened in unbelief is basically an uncircumcised heart.

He is resolving this dispute, not by exalting one flesh over another, but by bringing the righteousness after the flesh to its end, that the righteousness of faith, of the Spirit, might prevail and give life to all creation.

“For the flesh profits nothing. It is the Spirit who gives life.” (John 6:63)

So the current discourse is a war between the will of the flesh (that has taken on a Jewish form in hope of redeeming unbelieving Jews) and the will of the Spirit (those born of the Spirit, believers who are the circumcision and sealed with the Spirit). 

But the effect of the overcoming church is the redemption of all creation, so let the spirit have His way and not be stumbled.

for now, the consequences of this definition issue, is that many believers will even reject that Jesus was a Jew, because the definition of Jew is of the flesh and does not minister life, or offer freedom as in the Word. 
They may even hate everything “Jewish,” just as they hate their old man of the flesh, because it is defined and exalted that way to them. 

As the biblical Hebrew would regard the Gentile, so has it become today with the Jew because it is defined outside the circumcision of the Spirit and confidence in their flesh. But we have the liberty not to regard Christ after the flesh. We know him as the life giving Spirit ,  so we can minister to both the jew, greek and all, without this contention, all we see is the soul of someone either heading to eternal damnation or eternal life.

text:
Seitokai Ni Mo Ana Wa Aru!: Episode 2 

SB - Naoyuki Tatsuwa

ED - Naoyuki Tatsuwa & Takahiro Majima

Tatsuwa has returned for a second time to handle both SB and ED, with the help of Majima. Considering the current issues surrounding this production and how much it seems to be falling apart, the presence of additional assistant CADs gives this episode a much-needed edge in its overall quality.

Ryo Imamura remains the MAIN CAD, and his correction work stands above the rest as some of the best this year has to offer. The linework, particularly the shadows around the neck and nape, is another highlight in this man's career. Everything feels incredibly volumetric in the way it's processed, with Naoyuki and Majima also lending a hand. The first half of the episode was easily one of its most entertaining sections. Koma's introduction was adorable, and her bright, enthusiastic personality immediately made her stand out.

On the animation side, the episode remains just as strong as the first. With names such as Sheng Meng Chen, Kay Yu, Ningan, Ryo Imamura, Songlin Yao, Rei Kuroe, and others involved, the staff continues to deliver despite the circumstances surrounding the production. Kay Yu gets the standout highlight of the episode, with his character animation for Koma being particularly impressive. The way he handles her expressions, physicality, and movement—including the exaggerated breast motion—is absolutely worth looking out for.

The realism in the movement is something worth studying, and I hope to see Yu continue to develop his craft over time. The comedy remains strong, and so does the talent behind the production. Even through these treacherous circumstances, the staff continues to demonstrate just how much they can accomplish.

If the series can maintain this level of quality moving forward, it might end up being one of my favourite shows of 2026.

RATING: 8.6/10

RT @velitesgear | Full Text Article: https://t.co/Kd40EYljh1 | Author: @militarnyi B-52 Bombers to Receive LRASM Anti-Ship Missiles 
The U.S. Navy is preparing to award a contract to Lockheed Martin to integrate stealthy LRASM anti-ship missiles onto B-52 Stratofortress bombers.

The War Zone reported the development.

According to the publication, this reflects the U.S.military’s efforts to acquire new capabilities to counter increasingly powerful adversary naval forces, particularly in the Indo-Pacific region.

The latest notice from the U.S. Naval Air Systems Command says the command intends to negotiate with Lockheed Martin, the sole-source provider, before placing an order to integrate LRASM onto the B-52. The work will include missile software upgrades, relevant testing, repairs to test articles, and failure review board activities.

 An LRASM missile mounted under the wing of a U.S. Navy P-8A Poseidon. Photo credits: Naval News

The B-52 can already carry up to 20 air-launched cruise missiles from the AGM-158 Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile (JASSM) family, which served as the basis for the development of LRASM. Because the missiles share the same dimensions, the publication suggests the bomber could carry a similar number of anti-ship missiles.

The U.S. Air Force’s fiscal year 2027 budget request also outlines plans to integrate the latest versions of LRASM and JASSM onto the B-52. According to the document, the work is intended to enable the use of next-generation stealth cruise missiles against targets protected by sophisticated integrated air defense systems.

The work planned for fiscal year 2027 includes integrating the missiles’ onboard software with the B-52’s baseline software, verifying the safe separation of weapons from both underwing hardpoints and the internal launcher, upgrading weapons interfaces, and completing system safety testing.

LRASM Anti-Ship Missile

LRASM anti-ship missiles are designed to engage high-value surface combatants at long ranges. The missile’s guidance system combines inertial navigation with GPS updates and an imaging-infrared seeker that generates a target image and enables identification and acquisition during the terminal phase of flight.

The missile’s exact operational range has not been publicly disclosed. According to reports, the baseline LRASM can engage targets at ranges of 320–480 km, while the future C-3 version is expected to reach about 960 km. The missile is equipped with a 454 kg penetratingblast-fragmentation warhead.

The missile offers a high degree of autonomy thanks to its integrated route-planning system, linked to the onboard electronic support measures (ESM) system.

 An F/A-18F Super Hornet of the Royal Australian Air Force launches an LRASM anti-ship missile. Photo credits: RAAF

LRASM also features a data link that allows it to receive updated threat information in flight. It can also coordinate with other LRASM missiles during coordinated strikes.

Three versions of the missile are planned: LRASM 1.0, LRASM 1.1, and LRASM C-3. The baseline LRASM 1.0achieved early operational capability in 2019 and has already been integrated onto the B-1B Lancer and F/A-18E/F Super Hornet. Integration efforts are also underway for the F-15, F-35, P-8 Poseidon, and F-16. LRASM 1.1 is still undergoing Initial Operational Test and Evaluation (IOT&E).

text:
Introduction to "Obama's Dark Files"
The book will be published on October 20

Barack Obama left the White House wearing the same armor that had carried him through his entire political ascent: a story polished to hypnosis, repeated by so many obedient mouths that millions of Americans eventually mistook it for reality. On January 15, 2017, in his final 60 Minutes interview as president, he looked into the camera and told the country his administration had been among the most transparent in modern American history — nearly untouched by scandal, cleaner than the dirty business around it, elevated above Washington’s old corruptions. The press, which had spent eight years substituting admiration for scrutiny, received the line exactly as it had received everything else from him: with reverence. Hollywood had consecrated him. The Nobel committee had decorated him before he had proved anything. The image was perfect for an era addicted to packaging — the calm, cerebral, post-racial redeemer who arrived on cue to rescue America from the Bush years and governed with the kind of studied coolness that passes, in decadent times, for greatness.

It was a magnificent narrative. Like most magnificent narratives in politics, it depended on a selective relationship with truth.

The Obama years were never simply a presidency protected by a friendly press. They were a presidency built around narrative control, sustained by it, saved by it repeatedly. Facts were tolerated when they served the legend and buried when they threatened it. Obama’s defining talent was not speaking well, seducing donors, or igniting crowds. It was placing a moral halo around his own political machinery so effectively that his failures got marketed as sophistication, his evasions as nuance, his abuses as the regrettable necessities of enlightened governance.

Healthcare offered the purest early example. The lie was simple, memorable, and relentlessly repeated: if you like your doctor, you can keep your doctor; if you like your plan, you can keep your plan. He said it at rallies, press conferences, Sunday programs, and prime-time addresses — thirty-seven times in all — always in the calm, reassuring cadence presidents use when they want resistance to dissolve into trust. PolitiFact, no conservative operation, named it the Lie of the Year for 20131. What followed was equally familiar: plans canceled, networks shrank, doctors vanished from approved lists, premiums climbed, and families discovered the reassuring language had concealed a bureaucratic trapdoor beneath their feet. The companion promise — that the average family would save $2,500 a year — evaporated without ceremony, without admission, without correction. The pattern was set early: say what is needed, secure the objective, move on, and leave the public to discover the cost later.

Operation Fast and Furious followed the same template, at a higher human cost. Under Attorney General Eric Holder, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives ran an operation that deliberately allowed nearly 2,000 firearms to be purchased illegally and walked across the border into Mexico, on the theory that agents could trace them to cartel leadership. The theory collapsed. The tracking failed. The guns dispersed into one of the most violent criminal ecosystems in the hemisphere. One surfaced at the scene of Border Patrol Agent Brian Terry’s murder in December 2010. What followed in Washington was the now-familiar sequence: delay, evasion, contempt for oversight, and the institutional instinct to protect the apparatus before informing the public. Holder became the first sitting attorney general in American history held in contempt of Congress2. Mexico received nothing proportional to the damage done. Families on both sides of the border buried their dead while the governing class rehearsed its excuses.

The IRS scandal carried the same odor, on domestic soil. Beginning around 2010, the Internal Revenue Service systematically targeted tax-exempt applications from conservative organizations — Tea Party groups, patriot organizations, pro-Constitution activists — burying them in demands and delays across two consecutive election cycles. When Congress investigated, evidence vanished. The official at the center invoked the Fifth Amendment and retired with her pension intact. The full accounting belongs to a later chapter. What belongs here is the pattern: an agency whose legitimacy rests on perceived neutrality chose sides, chose them deliberately, and chose them at the moment it could inflict maximum political damage.

Solyndra arrived draped in environmental piety. Obama stood inside the company’s gleaming California factory in 2010 and declared it proof that his administration was financing the future. The federal government had already guaranteed $535 million in loans. Internal warnings about the company’s shaky finances had been noted and set aside. When Solyndra filed for bankruptcy in 2011, taxpayers absorbed the loss while certain well-positioned investors recovered funds ahead of the government. The administration called it the normal risk of innovation — a convenient phrase for half a billion dollars burned under the glow of political favoritism and the belief that moral posturing can disinfect corruption.

Overseas, the distance between mythology and record grew darker because bodies strip prose of its perfume. Obama campaigned as the man who would restore American moral credibility after the post-9/11 excesses. He then expanded the drone war to a scale that made his predecessor look restrained — authorizing roughly ten times the strikes Bush had approved across Pakistan, Yemen, and Somalia3, with civilian death estimates the administration disputed and investigators methodically documented. The administration protected itself with an accounting method as morally revealing as it was convenient: military-age males killed in a strike zone were classified as combatants unless explicit evidence later proved otherwise. The dead carried the burden of disproving their own execution.

Two of those dead were American citizens. Anwar al-Awlaki — born in New Mexico, later an al-Qaeda propagandist — died in a CIA drone strike in Yemen in September 2011, without indictment, without trial, without the constitutional machinery the United States invokes when it remembers its own principles. Two weeks later, a separate strike killed his sixteen-year-old son Abdulrahman. The boy had not been the target. When pressed, White House press secretary Robert Gibbs offered the coldest line of the entire administration: perhaps the child should have had a more responsible father. Washington rarely speaks that plainly unless it has stopped feeling the need to hide what it has become.

Syria delivered the next lesson. Obama drew his red line in August 2012 — chemical weapons use by Assad would trigger consequences. Assad used them in Ghouta in August 2013, killing hundreds. Children were photographed in rows, mouths foaming. Obama hesitated, drifted, and finally accepted a face-saving arrangement brokered by Russia. Assad kept his regime, the war raged on, and American credibility cashed its last check in the region. The lesson reached every government watching: American declarations under Obama came with expiration dates. The strategic vacuum that followed fed directly into ISIS’s expansion from insurgency to caliphate. Theatrical moral language at the front end, strategic collapse at the back end — and a media class eager to reframe the wreckage as complexity.

Then came Benghazi, which stripped the method completely bare. On September 11, 2012, militants linked to Ansar al-Sharia attacked the U.S. diplomatic compound and the CIA annex in Benghazi, Libya. Ambassador Christopher Stevens, Sean Smith, Tyrone Woods, and Glen Doherty were killed. The assault was organized, sustained, and immediately recognizable as terrorism. Within hours, senior American officials knew exactly what had happened. What followed was not fog of war. It was one of the most cynical acts of narrative management in recent American political history.

For nearly two weeks, the White House and the State Department promoted the fiction that a spontaneous protest over a YouTube video had spiraled into violence. Susan Rice repeated that explanation across five Sunday news programs on September 16, reciting the same script five times. There had been no protest, no mob, no accidental slide from outrage into chaos. A planned jihadist assault had killed four Americans on the anniversary of September 11, and the administration needed a politically safer story seven weeks before an election. Hillary Clinton knew the truth that same night. She emailed her daughter Chelsea that the compound had been hit by “an al-Qaeda-like group” — then watched her department blame inflammatory material on the Internet. The gap between Clinton’s private knowledge and her public account was not ambiguity. It was a decision. When Senator Ron Johnson pressed her on it in January 2013, she delivered the line that defined the affair: “What difference, at this point, does it make?” What many Americans heard was the voice of a ruling class offended that anyone still expected the truth after the funeral.

The domestic record added quieter corruptions. Not one senior Wall Street executive went to prison for the conduct that produced the worst financial crisis since 1929. The administration fined institutions delivered speeches about fairness, and avoided the personal accountability it lectured ordinary citizens to accept. Obama rewrote immigration policy by executive action after publicly acknowledging more than once that he lacked the constitutional authority to do it — then did it anyway. Obamacare waivers went to politically favored entities with a generosity that looked less like principle than selective indulgence.

The NSA collected phone metadata on millions of Americans, a fact Edward Snowden exposed in 2013 that the administration had been content to keep hidden. In the final months of 2016, officials including U.N. Ambassador Samantha Power submitted hundreds of requests to unmask American citizens named in classified intelligence reports — many of them connected to the incoming Trump transition team. Power later testified she had not personally made many of the requests attributed to her. Which only sharpened the central question: who had, under what authority, and for what purpose?

Nothing in this book rests on rumor, partisan hallucination, or the improvised fantasies of people who need conspiracies to explain history. What follows rests on congressional investigations, inspector general reports, court filings, declassified documents, and sworn testimony. These episodes were documented in plain sight and then softened by prestige media, neutralized by euphemism, or buried under the narcotic glamour of Obama’s image.

Taken together, they do not reveal a melodramatic villain. The truth is both more ordinary and more corrosive. They reveal a presidency that placed narrative above governance, image above truth, ideological ambition above institutional honesty, and self-protection above accountability. They reveal an elite culture that treats facts as raw material to be processed for public consumption, and regards citizens who insist on the difference as problems to be managed or ignored.

Obama was no fool, no passive vessel, no innocent symbol carried by history. He believed in himself, in his project, in the redemptive arc he was convinced he had been chosen to bend. Men of that conviction leave a deeper mess than ordinary cynics, because they do not conceal their ambitions. They sanctify them. By the end of eight years, the national debt had nearly doubled. The Middle East burned in ways still unresolved. Race relations, supposedly transcended by the symbolism of his election, curdled into something harder and more bitter. Democrats lost 958 state legislative seats across the country4 while magazines and award ceremonies celebrated his image.

To this already damning record must be added what may prove the most poisonous element of all: the emerging evidence surrounding the investigation that poisoned an American presidency before it began. The FBI opened Crossfire Hurricane as a full counterintelligence investigation on July 31, 2016, only three days after receiving information from an Australian diplomat concerning comments made by Trump campaign adviser George Papadopoulos. Durham concluded that the bureau had not performed the level of preliminary analysis he believed such an exceptionally sensitive investigation required. Declassified records also documented intelligence concerning an alleged Clinton campaign plan to connect Trump to Russia. CIA Director John Brennan briefed Obama and other senior officials about that intelligence; Durham explicitly declined to determine whether the underlying intelligence was accurate.5 Obama was briefed. Brennan was there. Biden was there. Comey was there. The result was one of the dirtiest political operations in modern American history — a fraud wrapped in the language of national security and sold to the public as patriotism. The Clinton-funded dossier, the laundering of fiction through intelligence networks, the contamination of the FBI, the effort to cripple a duly elected president before he could govern — none of this belongs to fantasy any longer. It belongs to the anatomy of a ruling class that decided the people could be overruled if the lie were made large enough.

At that point, Obama stopped resembling the healer the world had been sold. He started resembling the polished face of a system that preferred building its own deep state to surrendering its ideological grip on the country.

The facts are waiting. Turn the page.

Angela Paxton filed for divorce in July 2025 after 38 years of marriage. In the court petition she listed as grounds that Ken Paxton “has committed adultery,” stated the couple had not lived together as spouses since about June 1, 2024, and publicly described the filing as “on biblical grounds” in light of “recent discoveries.” Ken Paxton denied the adultery allegation in his response. This tracks earlier public allegations during his 2023 impeachment trial of an extramarital affair (linked at the time to donor Nate Paul); he was acquitted and denied the affair then. There is a formal legal accusation from his wife but no court finding or public admission of adultery so far. https://t.co/Vn1J7eAwuv 
“Pedophile” accusation (Adam Hoffman case)
Ken Paxton is not accused of being a pedophile. The claim refers to how his Attorney General’s office handled the prosecution of former Waco attorney Adam Hoffman.
Hoffman was charged with continuous sexual abuse of a young child (first-degree felony carrying up to life). The allegations involved repeated sexual abuse of a boy (a friend of Hoffman’s son) beginning around age 6–8, including genital contact and showing pornography. The 2025 trial ended in a hung jury (reported 7-5 for conviction). After the victim indicated he did not want to testify again, prosecutors offered a plea to two Class A misdemeanors (indecent assault and displaying harmful material to a minor). Hoffman signed a confession admitting he touched the victim’s genitals with sexual intent without consent; because the plea language did not specify the victim’s age, he avoided Texas sex-offender registration. An initial short jail proposal was rejected by the judge; Hoffman was sentenced to 60 days, served roughly 29 with good-time credit, surrendered his law license for five years, and is under a lifetime no-contact order. https://t.co/chTogHRZ2Z 
Prosecutors said they prioritized not forcing the child to testify a second time and had no path to a felony conviction without his testimony. Critics (including James Talarico and earlier John Cornyn) call it an overly lenient “sweetheart” deal, noting connections between Hoffman’s lawyers and Paxton donor Nate Paul; the victim’s mother expressed dissatisfaction with the outcome. Paxton has defended the office’s handling as the best available option given the hung jury and the child’s wishes. The core factual dispute is whether the plea appropriately balanced accountability against the child’s willingness to testify again.

text:
Former Waco attorney Adam Hoffman was charged with continuous sexual abuse of a young child (first-degree felony, potential 25 years to life). The victim was a friend of Hoffman’s son; alleged abuse spanned years starting around third grade. The local DA recused due to a prior conflict, so Texas AG Ken Paxton’s office took over the prosecution.
The 2025 trial ended in a hung jury (7-5 for guilty). Prosecutors said the victim did not want to testify again. They offered a plea to two Class A misdemeanors (indecent assault + display of harmful materials). Hoffman admitted in a judicial confession to touching the victim’s genitals with sexual intent and without consent. Because the admission did not specify the victim’s age, Texas law did not require sex-offender registration.
At the April 16, 2026 hearing, prosecutors initially recommended “time served” (one day already spent after the 2022 arrest). Visiting Judge Roy Sparkman rejected it, saying on the record: “One day. Seriously? Somebody has to sell me on the wisdom of it.” Prosecutors then proposed 30 days + law-license surrender + lifetime protective order. At the April 27 sentencing, the victim’s mother said 30 days was “not enough.” The judge imposed 60 days.
Hoffman was released May 25, 2026, after 29 days under the jail’s routine 2-for-1 good-conduct credit for misdemeanor inmates. He was not required to register as a sex offender in Texas (though Nebraska later required it after he moved). A lifetime no-contact order was imposed, and he was ordered to surrender his Texas law license (process was delayed).
Paxton’s office (line prosecutors Brenda Cantu and Dorian Cotlar) handled the case and plea. Defense counsel stated Paxton was not personally involved in negotiations. Paxton later publicly defended the outcome, citing the hung jury and the victim’s refusal to retestify, and saying the office “did our best” and prioritized protecting the child. He has described the result as 60 days served, though actual custody time was 29 days.
The “released after one day” claim refers only to the initial offer the judge rejected, not the final outcome.

text:
What if you could make your first $1,000 online without having 10,000 followers, a YouTube channel, or a popular personal brand?

You don't necessarily need an audience to make money online. 

One of the simplest business models to explore when you need revenue before building an audience is a service-based business.

Instead of creating a product and hoping people buy it, you offer a specific service that solves a problem for a customer.

For example:

- A small business in Texas needs someone to manage its social media accounts.
- A real estate agent in Canada needs help editing property listing videos.
- An e-commerce store in the UK needs product descriptions for its website.
- A startup in Australia needs a virtual assistant to manage appointments and emails.
- A US-based consultant needs help with email marketing or lead generation.

These businesses already have problems they need solved.

Your job is to identify a problem you can solve, communicate the value of your service, and find people willing to pay for it.

You don't have to wait until thousands of people follow you.

You can start by reaching out directly to potential clients.

Why is this business model attractive?

1. You can start without an existing audience.

You can use cold email, LinkedIn outreach, freelance marketplaces, networking, and direct business prospecting to find potential clients.

2. You can validate demand before investing heavily.

You don't need to spend months building a website, creating a course, or growing a YouTube channel before discovering whether people will pay for your offer.

You can test your service with potential customers first.

3. You can generate revenue relatively quickly.

If you identify a real problem, make a compelling offer, and find the right buyer, you may secure a paying client before building a substantial online presence.

Of course, getting clients isn't guaranteed, and your results will depend on your skills, offer, market, and sales process.

4. You can turn one-off projects into recurring revenue.

Imagine helping a real estate agent edit property videos.

Instead of charging for one video, you could offer a monthly package covering a specific number of videos.

The same applies to social media management, bookkeeping, email marketing, and virtual assistance.

Recurring contracts can make revenue more predictable.

If you need revenue before building an audience, this business model can be a sensible starting point.

But don't make the mistake of choosing a service simply because someone on YouTube claims it pays $5,000 a month.

Start by asking three questions:

1. What problem can I solve?

2. Who has this problem and can afford to pay for a solution?

3. How will I reach these people?

Don't spend months perfecting your logo, building an elaborate website, or creating business cards before speaking to potential customers.

Get evidence that people want what you're offering first.

If you want to start making money online, stop asking only: "What's the best online business to start?"

Ask a better question: "What problem can I solve for a specific group of people who are already willing to pay for a solution?"

That question can lead you toward a more practical business opportunity than chasing every trending online income idea.

text:
What if you could make your first $1,000 online without having 10,000 followers, a YouTube channel, or a popular personal brand?

You don't necessarily need an audience to make money online. 

One of the simplest business models to explore when you need revenue before building an audience is a service-based business.

Instead of creating a product and hoping people buy it, you offer a specific service that solves a problem for a customer.

For example:

- A small business in Texas needs someone to manage its social media accounts.
- A real estate agent in Canada needs help editing property listing videos.
- An e-commerce store in the UK needs product descriptions for its website.
- A startup in Australia needs a virtual assistant to manage appointments and emails.
- A US-based consultant needs help with email marketing or lead generation.

These businesses already have problems they need solved.

Your job is to identify a problem you can solve, communicate the value of your service, and find people willing to pay for it.

You don't have to wait until thousands of people follow you.

You can start by reaching out directly to potential clients.

Why is this business model attractive?

1. You can start without an existing audience.

You can use cold email, LinkedIn outreach, freelance marketplaces, networking, and direct business prospecting to find potential clients.

2. You can validate demand before investing heavily.

You don't need to spend months building a website, creating a course, or growing a YouTube channel before discovering whether people will pay for your offer.

You can test your service with potential customers first.

3. You can generate revenue relatively quickly.

If you identify a real problem, make a compelling offer, and find the right buyer, you may secure a paying client before building a substantial online presence.

Of course, getting clients isn't guaranteed, and your results will depend on your skills, offer, market, and sales process.

4. You can turn one-off projects into recurring revenue.

Imagine helping a real estate agent edit property videos.

Instead of charging for one video, you could offer a monthly package covering a specific number of videos.

The same applies to social media management, bookkeeping, email marketing, and virtual assistance.

Recurring contracts can make revenue more predictable.

If you need revenue before building an audience, this business model can be a sensible starting point.

But don't make the mistake of choosing a service simply because someone on YouTube claims it pays $5,000 a month.

Start by asking three questions:

1. What problem can I solve?

2. Who has this problem and can afford to pay for a solution?

3. How will I reach these people?

Don't spend months perfecting your logo, building an elaborate website, or creating business cards before speaking to potential customers.

Get evidence that people want what you're offering first.

If you want to start making money online, stop asking only: "What's the best online business to start?"

Ask a better question: "What problem can I solve for a specific group of people who are already willing to pay for a solution?"

That question can lead you toward a more practical business opportunity than chasing every trending online income idea.

Social media management? Virtual assistance? Video editing? Email marketing? Web design? Something else?
