### Core limitation from *Dastar*
The Supreme Court held that “origin of goods” in Lanham Act § 43(a) means the producer of the tangible product offered for sale, not the author or creator of the ideas, concepts, or communicative content embodied in it. Allowing reverse passing off claims to enforce attribution for creative authorship would effectively create a perpetual right outside the Copyright Act’s limited term and formalities. As a result, courts generally treat failure to credit the original author of expressive material as outside the scope of reverse passing off, whether the material is copyrighted or in the public domain.[](<https://t.co/NqrdBp4ILT>)

Post-*Dastar* decisions (including in the District of Oregon and other courts) have applied this to reject reverse passing off claims by authors seeking credit for protected elements of their copyrighted or copyrightable works. If the defendant is the producer of the copies or versions being distributed, lack of attribution alone typically does not support a Lanham Act reverse passing off theory.

### What still may be available for creative works
- **Copyright infringement**: Unauthorized copying, distribution, or creation of derivative works of copyrighted material remains the primary remedy. Copyright protects the expression itself (not ideas or facts) and does not require a trademark-style “origin” analysis.
- **False advertising under § 43(a)(1)(B)**: Narrower claims may survive if a defendant makes affirmative false or misleading statements in commercial advertising about the nature, characteristics, qualities, or source of the work (beyond mere failure to attribute authorship). Simple non-attribution of creative content is usually insufficient.
- **Contract, license, or other claims**: If there was an agreement requiring attribution, or if other statutory or common-law theories apply (e.g., certain state unfair-competition doctrines, though many track *Dastar*), those may be available depending on the facts.
- **Limited exceptions for tangible goods**: If the claim involves physical products that incorporate creative content (rather than pure communicative works), reverse passing off can sometimes still succeed when marks are removed from the tangible items themselves.

### Practical takeaway
For pure creative or intellectual works such as Blogspot writings, behavioral analyses, frameworks, videos, or similar content, reverse passing off is rarely a strong vehicle for enforcing attribution or ownership claims after *Dastar*. Copyright (or other tailored IP or contractual tools) is the more direct route. Outcomes still turn on specific facts—what was copied, how it was presented, commercial context, and the jurisdiction—and many such allegations remain unadjudicated public assertions rather than court findings.

🔹 Rather than seeking imprisonment for the teenagers, Levin wants them to learn about Judaism and antisemitism through engagement with the Jewish community.

🔹 The incident initially left his children afraid to return to school. However, seeing their father and neighbors stand together helped transform their fear into pride.

🔹 The community is now planning its largest Hanukkah celebration ever and encouraging residents to display signs reading, “I Stand With My Neighbors.”

text:
Dr. Robert Sungenis responded to my video on YouTube where I said I respectfully disagreed with Dr. E. Michael Jones on the Church teaching that Jews will convert at the end of time (after they bring forth and accept the Antichrist and Enoch and Elijah preaches to them) per Romans 11:25-26. 

Dr. Sungenis respectfully said this:

Hello. This is Robert Sungenis. I have not had the pleasure of meeting you yet. Thank you for your show. I would like to start a dialogue with you, if you are amenable. Dr. Jones and I have worked together for the last 25 years, especially on the "Jewish" question. I would like to say one thing upfront. You state in this video that a consensus of the Fathers consists of whether a Father has "dissented" from the common view. As I understand the doctrine of consensus from Trent and Vatican I, a consensus consists when the Fathers actually TEACH the idea in question. If we were to define consensus as including those who don't dissent, we could include anyone we like. When consensus is understood as those who actually teach the doctrine in question, then I can assure you that there is no consensus among the Fathers on the idea that there will be a mass conversion of the Jews at or near the Second coming, and that can be proven very easily. I will be publishing a paper on this very soon. Thank you. God be with you.

I responded with this:

Hello Dr. Sungenis. You're welcome! I have to say that I appreciate and respect the work you've done, just like I appreciate and respect the work of Dr. Jones. That being said, I have to point out that the Fathers do teach the idea in question. I made this video on Romans 11:25-26 a few months back:

https://t.co/g7pDudZWwn

And in this video I quote several Fathers. Here's a snippet of Church Father quotes I found:

St. Ambrose — Letter 34, §8
   “For when the fulness of the Gentiles shall be come in, then all Israel shall be saved. For what people will He not pardon when He even pardons that persecuting people, who said, Crucify Him, crucify Him, and, His blood be on us and on our children. But since even the heavenly creation is subject to vanity, albeit in hope, will not He Who is ' truly Mercy itself and the Redeemer of the world, suffer even the perfidy and insolence into which these men through the vanity of the world have fallen to obtain pardon?"

St. John Chrysostom — Homily 57 on Matthew, §1
   “Since when He says, Elias indeed comes, and will restore all things, He means Elias himself, and the conversion of the Jews which is then to take place; but when He says, Which was for to come, He calls John, Elias, with regard to the manner of his administration. Yea, and so the prophets used to call every one of their approved kings, David; and the Jews, rulers of Sodom, Isaiah 1:10 and sons of Ethiopians; Amos 9:7 because of their ways. For as the other shall be forerunner of the second advent, so was this of the first.”

St. Jerome — Letter 123, §13
   “At their birth was broken down that middle wall of partition which typified the division existing between the two peoples; Ephesians 2:14 while the binding of Zarah's hand with the scarlet thread even then marked the conscience of the Jews with the stain of Christ's blood. And how shall I speak of the whore married by the prophet who is a figure either of the church as gathered in from the Gentiles or — an interpretation which better suits the passage — of the synagogue? First adopted from among the idolaters by Abraham and Moses, this has now denied the Saviour and proved unfaithful to Him. Therefore it has long been deprived of its altar, priests, and prophets and has to abide many days for its first husband. For when the fullness of the Gentiles shall have come in, all Israel shall be saved.”

St. Augustine — The City of God, XX.29 & 30
   “It is a familiar theme in the conversation and heart of the faithful, that in the last days before the judgment the Jews shall believe in the true Christ, that is, our Christ, by means of this great and admirable prophet Elias who shall expound the law to them... And at or in connection with that judgment the following events shall come to pass, as we have learned: Elias the Tishbite shall come; the Jews shall believe; Antichrist shall persecute; Christ shall judge; the dead shall rise; the good and the wicked shall be separated; the world shall be burned and renewed.”

St. Cyril of Alexandria — Commentary on John, book II, introductory discussion of John 5
   “But the one believed with his whole house, and confessed that Jesus is God, while the others. who ought to have been astonished, straightway desire to kill, and persecute, as though blasphemously transgressing, their Benefactor, themselves against themselves pronouncing more shameful condemnation in that they are found to fall short of the understanding of the  aliens, and their piety towards Christ. And this it was which was spoken of them in the Psalms, as to our Lord Jesus, Thou shalt make them the back. For they having been set in the first rank because of the election of the fathers, will come last and after the calling of the Gentiles. For when the fulness of the Gentiles is come in, then shall all Israel be saved.”

St. Prosper of Aquitaine — The Call of All Nations, I.21; P. De Letter translation, p. 69
    “As we have already said above, 261 it is not given to any human study or genius to explore the decree and design according to which God, who is invariably good, invariably just, ever foreknowing, ever omnipotent, hath concluded all in unbelief, that He may have mercy on all; yet He delayed for centuries, while He was educating Israel, to enlighten the countless peoples of infidels; and now He allows that same Israel to go blind till the universality of the Gentiles enter the fold. He allows so many thousands of this people to be born and die to be lost, when only those whom the end of the world will find alive will attain salvation.”

St. Gregory the Great — Moralia in Job, XXXV.24 & 26
    “For though Holy Church now loses many by the stroke of temptation, yet in the end of this world she receives those things that are her own, twofold, when, having received the Gentiles in full number, all Judaea also which shall then be found, agrees to run to her faith... But these words which are subjoined attest that they rather announce the conversion of the Jewish people at the end of this world. For it is added; There came to him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all that knew him before, and did eat bread with him in his house. For then do His brethren and sisters come to Christ, when as many as shall have been found of the Jewish people are converted.”

St. Isidore of Seville — On the Catholic Faith against the Jews, II.5, chapter heading; translation from the Latin
    “At the end of the world the Jews will believe in Christ.”

St. Bede — Explanation of the Apocalypse, book I, on Revelation 3:10; Edward Marshall translation (1878), p. 26
    “But as to this, it is believed that the wicked Jews will be deceived as well as deceive, but that others will understand the law spiritually through the instruction of the great prophet Elijah, and will be incorporated among the members of the Church, and bravely overcome the enemy.”

This is just a sample. I found many more. But this should at least suffice to show that there is a consensus amongst the Church Fathers. Now the real question is this: Is this just a common opinion or is this unanimous consent? 

The bar for unanimous consent isn't that we have certainty that every Church Father taught it. That would be an impossible bar to overcome because there are quite a few Church Fathers that have little to no writings that exist.

So the bar has to be that we cannot find a Church Father that explicitly dissents to this position (I know both Sts. Augustine and Jerome offer other alternatives in their writings, i.e. "All Israel shall be saved" could mean that all Jews ad Gentiles in Christ as saved, but neither dissent to this position that the Jews will coporately convert, as shown above).

And I have yet to find one Church Father that diseents to this common opinion. And trust me, I have looked. I have probably the most extensive free source of the Catholic Adversus Judaeos Tradition on the Internet:

https://t.co/yjkrHr9s3S

That being said, Dr. Sungenis, you've been studying this issue for longer than me, so maybe you've found a source (or more) that I have not found that proves this is just a common opinion and not unanimous consent (we only need 1 dissenting Father here).

So yes, I would be interested to know if you have found such sources, and if that's the case, then I will humbly change my view to that it's just a common opinion of the Fathers that the Jews will corporately convert at the end of time (after they bring forth the Antichrist, whom they will accept, and after Elijah and Enoch preach to them, of course). 

All the best, and God bless, Dr. Sungenis!

I am actually very much interested in having this discussion. Everyone knows that Dr. Sungenis and I (and Dr. Jones for that matter) are all defenders of the Adversus Judaeos tradition and against Neo-Judaizing in the Church. So I will be very eager to hear what Dr. Sungenis has to say.

text:
The Opening Edge
Sunday Futures Open 
October 11, 2026

Tonight’s open enters a heavily recalibrated market landscape following Friday’s massive October World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates (WASDE) report shock and late week cross asset re positioning. 

On Friday, the USDA unexpectedly raised its national corn yield estimate from 178.5 to 181.2 bushels per acre. This sharply contradicted market expectations and sent December corn futures tumbling more than 4% (-20.50 cents) to close at $4.79 3/4. 

The agricultural supply shock spilled across wheat contracts, while soybeans managed a resilient green close above $13.08.

In macro assets, S&P 500 futures (/ES) capped off Friday with a solid +0.64% surge to settle at 7,866.00, buoyed by dip buying in mega cap technology and stabilizing corporate earnings expectations. 

WTI crude oil (/CL) held relatively steady near $91.66/bbl, keeping energy risk premiums firm as middle east transit monitoring continues. 

Meanwhile, December gold (/GC) staged its biggest daily percentage gain in over five weeks on Friday, leaping 1.85% to settle at $4,233.70/oz as safe haven momentum returned despite sticky long term Treasury yields.

The primary tell out of the gate tonight is WASDE Supply Shock Digestion vs. Equity Index Breakout Momentum. If /ES defends Friday's 7,866 settlement floor while crude oil (/CL) holds $91.50, risk on momentum will attempt to extend toward new local highs. 

However, on the ag floor, traders will watch whether commercial end users step in to stem the corn liquidation or if fund managers press short exposure below $4.80. Watch the first 30 to 60 minutes closely; with supply balance sheets freshly updated, opening order flow will be fast and reactive.

Energy Desk

/CL Crude Oil
November WTI crude enters the session after settling Friday at $91.66/bbl (+0.19%). The market continues to balance physical transit risks in the Middle East against steady non OPEC output assumptions.
What to watch: The size of the initial gap at the bell, and whether commercial buyers step in to defend the $91.00–$91.50 pivot zone.
Comments: Range testing mode. Physical supply concerns continue to floor the market, though demand uncertainties keep rallies contained.
Opening Edge: If /CL holds above $92.00 through the first 30 minutes, expect momentum buyers to target a fast recovery drive toward $93.50.

/NG Natural Gas
Natural gas enters the session trading near $2.85/MMBtu, balancing shoulder season domestic storage injections against regional temperature trends.
What to watch: Updated mid October weather maps and storage injection estimates across the central U.S.
Comments: Thin liquidity alert. Watch for erratic stop runs if overnight trading overlaps with shifting regional weather forecasts.
Opening Edge: If /NG clears and defends $2.90 out of the gate, look for speculative longs to drive a fast push toward $3.00.

Metals Desk
/GC Gold
December gold futures enter tonight's trade at $4,233.70/oz after a strong 1.85% Friday surge (+ $76.80), executing a sharp technical bounce off recent multi month lows.
What to watch: U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) behavior and Asian cash session physical demand following Friday's explosive safe haven rally.
Comments: Safe haven rebound. Strong central bank demand and geopolitical hedging continue providing a solid floor beneath paper allocations.
Opening Edge: A clean hourly close above $4,240 early tonight confirms institutional buyers are actively extending Friday's breakout momentum.

/SI Silver
Silver enters the session hovering near $62.40/oz, tracking gold's broader Friday rally while reacting to industrial demand expectations out of global manufacturing centers.
What to watch: Relative strength versus gold out of the gate and speculative industrial positioning in early Asian trade.
Comments: High beta mover. Silver remains hyper sensitive to moves in real yields and dollar fluctuations.
Opening Edge: If silver clears and defends $63.00 early tonight, expect speculative long volume to re accelerate toward $64.20.

Equity Index Desk
/ES S&P 500 Futures
S&P 500 futures enter the open on a firm footing after settling Friday at 7,866.00 (+0.64%), holding technical momentum as buyers defend key support levels.
What to watch: Whether overnight trade defends Friday's 7,866 settlement baseline or leaks back toward the 7,820 support cluster.
Comments: Tech led momentum. Equity bulls are maintaining control as long as key moving averages hold.
Opening Edge: Holding above 7,860 in the first hour confirms institutional buyer support, setting up an early push toward the 7,900 handle.

/NQ Nasdaq Futures
Nasdaq 100 futures enter the session following a strong late week performance, led by mega cap tech stability and hardware infrastructure demand.
What to watch: 10-year Treasury yield direction in early Asian trade and relative performance against /ES.
Comments: Growth proxy. Highly sensitive to any sudden upward momentum in long term bond yields.
Opening Edge: If /NQ holds above Friday's highs in the first 30 minutes, momentum algorithms will target an immediate breakout extension.

/YM Dow Futures
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures enter the open after capping off a steady Friday session, supported by blue chip financial and industrial lines.
What to watch: Sector rotation between traditional value and growth lines at the bell.
Comments: Defensive indicator. Essential for confirming if broader market participation is supporting the rally.
Opening Edge: If /YM reclaims key overhead resistance early, expect value seeking accounts to stabilize index breadth.

/RTY Russell 2000 Futures
The "Truth Teller." Small caps enter the session acting as the primary gauge for how small business balance sheets absorb current rate parameters.
What to watch: Early market breadth clues and short covering interest at the open.
Opening Edge: If /RTY leads an overnight /ES bounce, it confirms authentic, broad based market risk appetite.

Monday's Opening Edge
Grain Desk
/ZC Corn
December corn futures enter the week in a severe technical repair posture after plunging 20.50 cents on Friday to settle at $4.79 3/4. The market is digesting the USDA's shock yield hike to 181.2 bu/acre and an expanded 1.8 billion bushel ending stocks forecast.
What to watch: Early week harvest progress reports, commercial end user buying at sub $4.80 levels, and fund short positioning.
Comments: WASDE shock aftermath. The 2.7-bushel yield surprise forces the market to price in heavy fall harvest supply pressure.
Opening Edge: If December corn holds above $4.78 at the 8:00 PM ET reopen, look for commercial end users to step in and spark a corrective bounce toward $4.88.

/ZW Wheat
December Chicago SRW wheat enters the session sitting at $6.71 00 (-12.25 cents on Friday), caught in the WASDE supply drag alongside Kansas City HRW ($7.19 1/4).
What to watch: International export tenders, Black Sea shipping headlines, and southern plains moisture updates.
Comments: Spillover pressure. Wheat is balancing expanding domestic corn supplies against global export competition.
Opening Edge: If wheat reclaims $6.78 in the first hour of ag trade, expect fund short covering to spill over and stabilize the grain floor.

/ZS Soybeans
January soybeans enter tonight's trade at $13.08 3/4 (+4.50 cents on Friday), defying the broader WASDE ag sell off thanks to firm export demand and tight crush margins.
What to watch: 8:00 PM ET weather map updates for South America and flash export sales announcements to China.
Comments: Ag floor relative strength leader. Soybeans showed impressive structural resilience during Friday's WASDE release.
Opening Edge: Holding above $13.05 at the reopen signals continued commercial support, setting up a push toward $13.20.

Livestock Desk
/LE Live Cattle
October live cattle futures enter the week backed by tight domestic animal allocations and steady boxed beef cutout values.
What to watch: Cash trade expectations for the coming week and packer margin trends.
Comments: Structural firming. Tight domestic cattle numbers continue supporting the long term trend.
Opening Edge: If October live cattle defend $218.00 out of the gate, expect buyers to target a retest of last week's highs near $220.50.

/GF Feeder Cattle
October feeder cattle enter the week watching the grain floor closely, as Friday's 20-cent crash in corn futures offers immediate margin relief to feedlot operations.
What to watch: The 8:00 PM ET ag reopen. Sharp corn weakness should provide direct tailwinds for feeder execution.
Comments: High margin sensitivity. Lower feed input costs are a major structural positive for feeder cattle.
Opening Edge: If corn futures stay suppressed under $4.82 at 8:00 PM ET, look for feeder cattle to catch an aggressive short covering bid.

/HE Lean Hogs
October lean hogs enter the week navigating seasonal pork cutout trends and packer slaughter pace.
Comments: Technical range. Watch packer margin adjustments and cutout movement.
Opening Edge: If /HE holds above $77.50 early, expect range bound traders to step in for an early push toward $78.80.

Things To Watch Immediately After Open
Does Crude Oil (/CL) hold the $91.50 support floor or trigger a secondary pullback?

Does /ES defend Friday's 7,866 breakout level or test lower support?

Do Gold (/GC) and Silver (/SI) build on Friday's +1.85% rally or face Asian profit taking?

How does December Corn (/ZC) react at the 8:00 PM ET reopen following Friday's 4% WASDE crash?

Do Feeder Cattle (/GF) jump out of the gate to price in lower corn input expenses?

Opening Levels That Matter
Baseline Levels: S&P 500 futures at 7,866.00, WTI Crude at $91.66, Dec Gold at $4,233.70, Dec Corn at $4.79 3/4.

S&P 500 Key Floor: 7,820.00; key technical support level to keep short term bulls in control.

WTI Crude Pivot: $91.50; holding above keeps energy risk premiums intact.

Corn WASDE Support: $4.75.00; critical psychological and technical floor following the October yield surprise.

The Bottom Line
Tonight’s session hinges on how the commodity and financial pits digest Friday's WASDE supply shock alongside broad equity breakout strength. Keep your eyes squarely on the relationship between /ZC Corn, /GF Feeder Cattle, and /ES. If equities hold 7,860 while feeder cattle catch a bid on cheapened grain, macro risk appetite remains solid. Let the opening noise clear out, avoid chasing Sunday gaps, and execute cleanly at your hard technical levels.

Futures trading involves significant risk. Information provided is for educational purposes only.

text:
My fellow Texans.  A quick 30 second search reveals the truth behind the ad nauseum ads run by anti-Paxton PACs.  Educate yourself...
The current “Paxton sweetheart deal” controversy centers on a 2026 plea agreement in the Adam Hoffman child sexual abuse case handled by the Texas Attorney General’s office under Ken Paxton. It has been a major attack line in the Texas U.S. Senate race (Paxton as the Republican nominee vs. Democrat James Talarico; also used earlier by John Cornyn in the primary).​
Dailykos
Key Facts from Court Proceedings and Reporting
Defendant and charges: Adam Hoffman, a former Waco attorney, was charged with continuous sexual abuse of a young child (first-degree felony, punishable by 25 years to life). The victim (a friend of Hoffman’s son) alleged repeated sexual assaults and being shown pornography during sleepovers over about three years, beginning when the boy was roughly 6–7 (third grade) and continuing until around age 10. Hoffman was arrested in 2022.​
Texastribune
Prosecution: Paxton’s office took over after the local McLennan County DA recused due to prior contact with Hoffman.
Trial: June 2025 ended in a hung jury (reported as 7-5 for guilty after lengthy deliberations). There were issues with the original investigation (non-specialist interview of the child) and some inconsistencies in the child’s testimony, common challenges in delayed-disclosure child abuse cases.​
Texastribune
Plea offer and resolution: After the victim indicated he did not want to testify again, prosecutors offered a deal reducing the charge to two Class A misdemeanors: indecent assault and displaying harmful materials to a minor. Hoffman admitted in a judicial confession to touching the victim’s genitals with sexual intent without consent. The victim’s age was not specified in the plea documents, so Texas sex offender registration was not required.
The initial proposal was essentially time served (one day previously spent in jail). Visiting Judge Roy Sparkman rejected it, stating something along the lines of “One day. Seriously? Somebody has to sell me on the wisdom of it.” The deal was revised; Sparkman ultimately imposed 60 days in jail, required Hoffman to surrender his law license for at least five years, and imposed a lifetime protective order. Hoffman was released after about 29 days under local good-time policies.​
Snopes
Victim’s family position: The mother was involved in discussions and initially went along with aspects of the resolution but later said the family was put in an “impossible situation,” that the outcome was not enough, and that prosecutors indicated they could proceed without her agreement while preferring her support.​
Texastribune
Paxton’s Office Explanation vs. Criticisms
Prosecutors (and Paxton in public remarks) have said they faced no reliable path to a felony conviction without the child’s testimony, prioritized avoiding further trauma to the victim, secured an admission of guilt plus some jail time, and noted the hung jury showed the case was not a lock. Paxton has framed the one-day criticism as misrepresenting the final outcome (“They served 60 days”).​
Dailykos
Critics (Cornyn, Talarico, some local officials, and the judge) call it an “Epstein-style” or extreme “sweetheart” deal: a life-eligible felony reduced to short misdemeanor jail with no registry. They highlight the initial one-day proposal, the shared defense attorney connection (Hoffman’s lawyer Gerry Morris also represented Nate Paul, the donor central to Paxton’s earlier impeachment), and argue it undercuts Paxton’s tough-on-crime posture. The Texas Tribune and local outlets (KWTX, etc.) reported the judge saw a pattern of lenient resolutions after mistrials in other AG-handled cases.​
Dallasobserver
Context and Caveats
Plea deals (including reductions when re-trial risks re-traumatizing a child witness or when evidence is imperfect) are routine in sexual abuse prosecutions; experts note that forcing testimony can be

text:
🚨 𝗡𝗔𝗩𝗜𝗚𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗡𝗙𝗢𝗥𝗗/𝗘𝗟𝗦𝗘𝗩𝗜𝗘𝗥 𝗧𝗢𝗣 𝟮% 𝗟𝗜𝗦𝗧: 𝗠𝗲𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗰𝘀, 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗹-𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗹𝗱 𝗕𝗶𝗮𝘀𝗲𝘀, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗗𝘂𝗮𝗹-𝗗𝗿𝗶𝗳𝘁 𝗙𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗲𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸

The annual release of the Stanford/Elsevier “World’s Top 2% Scientists” list sparks a familiar wave of university announcements and professional celebrations.

For researchers, inclusion can signify meaningful recognition of years of scholarly work. For institutions, it becomes a prominent part of their public identity.

That recognition deserves respect and accurate interpretation.

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘀𝗲 𝗺𝗲𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗰𝘀 𝗮𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗵𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗻𝘀 𝘄𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝗯𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗴𝗼𝗮𝗹?
🔎 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗟𝗜𝗦𝗧 𝗠𝗘𝗔𝗦𝗨𝗥𝗘𝗦

The database uses Scopus citation records and a composite citation indicator called the c-score. Developed by John P. A. Ioannidis and collaborators, the c-score combines six indicators:

• Total citations.
• The h-index.
• The co-authorship-adjusted hm-index.
• Citations to single-authored papers.
• Citations to papers where the researcher is the single or first author.
• Citations to papers where the researcher is the single, first, or last author.

The final three categories overlap. They incorporate authorship position into the assessment, although author order cannot fully establish intellectual contribution, leadership, or the quality of mentorship. 

The database provides separate views of career-long and single-year citation impact. “Single-year” refers to citations received in that year, including citations to older publications.

Selection includes researchers among the top 100,000 by c-score, with or without self-citations, or within the top 2% of their main subfield. 

This is a substantial effort to make citation assessment more informative. Its interpretation still requires judgment.

Indeed, the database’s own description cautions against treating inclusion as conclusive evidence of excellence and explicitly states that absence does not mean a researcher does poor work. 

⚖️ 𝗪𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗕𝗟𝗜𝗡𝗗 𝗦𝗣𝗢𝗧𝗦 𝗥𝗘𝗠𝗔𝗜𝗡

𝗙𝗶𝗲𝗹𝗱 𝗱𝗶𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲𝘀

The database accounts for scientific fields and subfields. These comparisons help address differences in citation density. However, broad rankings still require caution because citation practices, research communities, and opportunities for visibility vary even within subfields. 

𝗖𝗮𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗿 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝘂𝗺𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗮𝗱𝘃𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗴𝗲

Career-long indicators inevitably reflect the time available to accumulate citations. A single-year view helps, but established researchers also have a larger body of earlier work available for citation. 

Success can also create further opportunities. The “Matthew effect” describes this accumulation of advantage; research on science funding has documented that an early funding success can influence subsequent funding opportunities. 

𝗨𝗻𝗲𝗾𝘂𝗮𝗹 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗰𝗵 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗱𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀

A well-funded laboratory and a clinician–scientist with limited protected research time operate under different conditions.

Fair evaluation should consider access to funding, infrastructure, collaboration, and publishing opportunities. It should also recognize scholarship that addresses local needs, including work whose importance may be greater than its international citation visibility.

𝗖𝗶𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗶𝗽𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

The database reports indicators with and without self-citations and provides information to help identify unusual citation patterns. These are useful safeguards.

Nevertheless, excessive reciprocal citation and organized citation farming can distort bibliometric metrics. The database’s authors acknowledge that removing self-citations alone may not resolve every problem; suspicious patterns require individual examination. 

🧭 𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗬𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗠𝗬 𝗗𝗨𝗔𝗟-𝗗𝗥𝗜𝗙𝗧 𝗙𝗥𝗔𝗠𝗘𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞

My Dual-Drift Framework distinguishes between two problems: Evidence Drift and Causal Maturation Drift. Here, I use it as a conceptual lens for research assessment. 

𝗘𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗗𝗿𝗶𝗳𝘁: 𝗪𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺 𝗲𝘅𝗰𝗲𝗲𝗱𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗲𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲

Evidence Drift occurs when a finding is extended to a stronger or different claim without sufficient evidentiary support. 

When applied to rankings, the concern arises when “high citation impact” is treated as a claim of superior methodological quality, clinical judgment, or societal benefit.

For example, an institution might use the number of listed researchers to imply it provides better patient care. Establishing that claim requires evidence about patient care itself.

Similarly, a researcher’s citation rank cannot establish whether a particular study supports a causal conclusion. That judgment requires examining the study’s design, analysis, and limitations.

𝗖𝗮𝘂𝘀𝗮𝗹 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗗𝗿𝗶𝗳𝘁: 𝗪𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗰𝗵 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝘂𝗺𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗲𝘀 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗼𝗹𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗸𝗲𝘆 𝘂𝗻𝗰𝗲𝗿𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘁𝘆

Causal Maturation Drift concerns a research trajectory that continues to elaborate on an established signal without proportionate progress toward resolving consequential questions about temporal, causal, comparative, long-term, or implementation issues. 

Applied here, I would ask whether citation rewards encourage researchers to stay within productive, familiar questions while more difficult questions remain unanswered.

In pediatric dentistry, for example, a research program might repeatedly document well-known risk associations. The next consequential question may be whether acting on that knowledge improves children’s outcomes, access to care, or equity.

Assessing progress therefore requires examining what successive studies actually resolve. Valuable replication and foundational discovery remain essential; the question is whether the next study addresses a meaningful uncertainty.

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗱𝗼 𝘄𝗲 𝗻𝗼𝘄 𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗱, 𝗱𝗲𝗰𝗶𝗱𝗲, 𝗼𝗿 𝗱𝗼 𝗯𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗯𝗲𝗰𝗮𝘂𝘀𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗰𝗵?

🧠 𝗪𝗛𝗘𝗡 𝗦𝗖𝗢𝗥𝗘𝗦 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗥𝗧 𝗧𝗢 𝗦𝗛𝗔𝗣𝗘 𝗣𝗨𝗥𝗣𝗢𝗦𝗘

An evaluation system can influence which questions researchers feel able to pursue.

If promotion and recognition depend heavily on citation performance, a scholar may feel pressured to choose a fashionable, readily publishable topic over a difficult question that requires years of investigation.

The concern about research culture extends well beyond this list. Wellcome’s research culture survey documented researchers’ concerns about an emphasis on metrics, intense competition, and constraints on creativity. 

This raises a deeply personal question:

“Am I choosing this research because it addresses an important problem, or because it offers the safest path to recognition?”

Academic systems should foster curiosity, integrity, mentorship, and the courage to pursue consequential questions.

🌱 𝗠𝗢𝗩𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗕𝗘𝗬𝗢𝗡𝗗 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗣𝗘𝗥𝗖𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗜𝗟𝗘

Universities and funders should use bibliometrics alongside informed assessment of the work itself. This approach aligns with the Leiden Manifesto’s call for responsible evaluation guided by expert judgment. 

That assessment should ask:

• Is the research rigorous, transparent, and reproducible?
• Are its claims proportionate to the evidence?
• Does it address meaningful unanswered questions?
• Does it advance understanding or improve decisions?
• Does it contribute to patient care, public benefit, teaching, or mentorship where those contributions are relevant?
• Does it recognize local needs and the conditions under which the work was produced?

My call is to celebrate recognition while keeping the scientific purpose clearly in view.

𝗥𝗲𝘄𝗮𝗿𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗮𝗱𝘃𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲𝘀 𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴, 𝗿𝗲𝗱𝘂𝗰𝗲𝘀 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗲𝗾𝘂𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝘂𝗻𝗰𝗲𝗿𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘁𝘆, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲𝘀 𝗹𝗶𝘃𝗲𝘀.

💬 Has the emphasis on citation rankings changed the questions you—or your institution—choose to pursue? What valuable contributions remain insufficiently recognized?

text:
1. Body Armor & Helmets
Steel Jack / Corslet (Cuirass): A heavy iron or steel breastplate and backplate worn over a padded doublet. Designed to stop iron-tipped arrows, musket ball fragments, and close-quarters hand strikes.

Jack of Plate / Buff Coat: A thick, layered leather coat (often stiffened oxhide) or a canvas jacket lined with overlapping small iron plates sewn inside. Extremely common among light infantry and veteran lieutenants because it offered maneuverability while providing arrow and blade defense.

Cabacet / Morion Helmet: A steel open-faced helmet with a prominent crest along the top and a brim curved down on the sides. It protected against overhead strikes and arrows while preserving full visibility and hearing during fort perimeter watches.

Target (Buckler/Shield): Small round steel or heavy leather shields were explicitly listed in Virginia Company military inventories for close-quarters fighting inside stockades and dense bush.

2. Firearms & Matchlocks
Matchlock Musket / Caliver: The standard infantry longarm of the era, firing a heavy lead ball (typically around .69 to .75 caliber). It relied on a slow-burning match cord held in a serpentine cock to ignite the priming powder.

Bandolier & Powder Flask ("The Twelve Apostles"): A leather shoulder belt carrying a series of wooden or tin charger bottles pre-measured with gunpowder charges, along with a secondary powder horn for fine priming powder and a lead ball pouch.

Rest: A wooden stake with a broad steel fork at the top used to steady the heavy matchlock barrel when firing over the fort’s wooden palisade walls.

3. Close-Quarters Edged Weapons
Broadsword / Basket-Hilted Sword / Rapier: A sturdy, double-edged cut-and-thrust sword worn at the waist, vital for close-quarters combat inside the fort when firearms could not be reloaded in time.

Dagger / Dirk: Worn on the opposite hip for hand-to-hand defense.

Boarding Axe / Hand Axe: A heavy tactical hand axe carried on the belt. As recorded during the 1622 attack at Causey's Care, this was a standard piece of gear for a fighting man—used both as a camp/fortification tool and a lethal close-quarters weapon.

Pike / Halberd: Long polearms kept in the Jamestown fort armor stores. Non-commissioned officers and lieutenants frequently carried halberds (a polearm combining an axe blade, spear point, and beak hook) to command perimeter ranks and keep attackers at bay along narrow palisade gates.

text:
Greenbrier Bigfoot Photo — 2008

This “Bigfoot” photo has been floating around the internet for years and I never had a clue about its origin — until now.

On October 12, 2008, a trail camera belonging to the Greenbrier Sporting Club at White Sulphur Springs, Greenbrier County, West Virginia, took this black-and-white still. The club sits on the grounds of The Greenbrier, in the southern Alleghenies. Their outdoor-pursuits team had cameras on the property to count deer and bear. A huge thanks goes out to @Bigfoot_Doc for pointing me in the right direction.

The club’s own video, uploaded September 8, 2010, confirms the location. Jacob stands just off the golf course on the Summit Trail, over what he says is left of the stump, and offers a kid in a costume, an employee trick, or a Sasquatch. He does not pick one. The club played the clip for a laugh rather than as a sighting report. A trail-cam still, later used in their own promo. No hole number, and no coordinate for the stump. The course itself sits near 37.77° N, 80.33° W. The camera was just off that course. That is as close as the record gets.

On this frame the figure and the wood read as one object to me. The broken grain of the stump runs up into what the eye finishes as a torso. No separate arms I can defend, no feet, no second frame, and no return photo of the stump with the subject gone. By the time the club walked out two years later, the stump had been broken down.

I put a frame from the 2010 video next to the still to get a sense of scale. Jacob is standing over the remnant, and the trail cam was looking from another angle, so the comparison cannot be exact. Close enough, though. I believe the figure’s size reads between the man’s shoulders and full height, certainly not taller. That leaves room for someone standing behind the stump. A kid, or a crouching adult, fits the height better than a full-grown Sasquatch would. Jacob only offered those three: a member’s kid in a Halloween costume, an employee playing a trick, or the real thing. He did not mention the possibility that it was just the stump itself. If this is a Bigfoot, it is a small one. 

There’s no way for me to be sure but I’m going to chalk this one up on my scorecard as a “stump-squatch”, i.e. pareidolia. What do you say?

text:
Maci 💋 My POV
Sunday, October 11, 2026
Breckenridge, Colorado

Good morning from the mountains! ☕❤️

I'm sitting on the deck wrapped in a blanket, drinking coffee and watching the sunlight reach the Rockies. Snow on the peaks, patches beneath the evergreens, and golden aspens scattered across the mountainside.

It's freezing out here (31º). I'm not moving.

Edgar, you wonderful, wonderful man. ❤️ Let me explain.

Yesterday started ridiculously early in La Jolla. Edgar and I managed a workout before leaving, Jenny had our travel arrangements organized, and Mia was still wondering whether she'd packed enough.

Jack showed up with one small bag.

"That's it?" Mia asked.

"Yep."

"What if you need something?"

"I'll buy it."

Remember that conversation. 😂

On the flight, Jenny was reviewing Edgar's schedule while he worked on his laptop. She's settling into her new position as his and Spencer's executive assistant beautifully.

At one point, she placed breakfast beside him.

"Eat."

"In a minute."

She lowered his laptop screen.

"Now, please."

He looked at me.

I smiled. "Don't involve me. I'm enjoying this."

He ate.

Spencer, your girl, Jenny, is doing very well. 💋

We landed in Denver around 11 a.m. and headed to the Denver Zoo for the Collins company family afternoon.

Employees, spouses, children, games, prizes, and grown men who took competing against little kids seriously.

I loved watching Edgar with everyone.

He was handing out prizes, teasing employees, remembering their children's names, and laughing with people who have helped him build the company.

One little boy asked if he owned the zoo.

"No."

"Could you buy it?"

"I don't think they'd sell me the elephants."

The boy considered that.

"Could you ask?"

I lost it. 😂 I love a mind of a child.

Jenny was introduced to everyone as Edgar and Spencer's new executive assistant. 

A few employees had never met me in person, either. Nearly TWO YEARS, and we're still doing introductions!

One employee's wife asked what I did.

"I'm Head of Staff."

"Oh! So you work closely with Edgar?"

"Very."

Edgar walked up behind me.

"She also keeps me humble."

"That's an entirely separate position," I told her. "And considerably more demanding."

Jenny joined us.

"I can confirm that."

I looked at her.

"Careful, Jenny. You're still on your probation."

Edgar laughed.

The poor woman looked between the three of us and started laughing, too. I suspect she went home with a few questions. 

People asked about Spencer, too, wondering where she was. They clearly missed seeing her. 

Mia and Jack were introduced to everyone, and Jack made friends within minutes. Mia ended up helping a little girl win one of the games.

Afterward, we wandered around the zoo. My first visit!

Mia and Jack spent most of the afternoon holding hands. She'd stop to admire an animal, he'd slip his arms around her, and they'd get distracted talking before moving along.

Jenny walked beside Edgar, asking about the employees she’d met. She wanted to know how everyone fit into the business. Edgar was more than happy to explain. 

"Do all your employees adore you this much?" Jenny asked.

“Do all your employees adore you this much?” Jenny asked.

“Ask them again on Monday.”

I leaned around him.

“Jenny, negotiate your next raise before then.”

She slipped her arm through his.

"I think I negotiated rather well."

I raised an eyebrow.

Oh, she's learning. 😂

We left the zoo around 4:30, and I assumed we were heading downtown to Edgar's penthouse.

Except we kept driving west. 

"Edgar, where are we going?"

"Home."

"Your penthouse is behind us."

"I know."

Jenny checked her phone.

"Wait. I have the Denver address."

"Change of plans."

"I'm your executive assistant!"

"Yes."

"Shouldn't I know where we're staying?"

"You will."

I was laughing so hard Jenny threatened to resign. 

As we climbed into the mountains, the scenery became spectacular. Golden aspens covered the hillsides, and snow appeared on the higher peaks.

Then I caught on.

"Edgar, are we going to Aspen?"

"No."

"Where?"

"Breckenridge."

He glanced at me.

"You wanted aspens and snow."

I stared at him.

He smiled.

Oh, that man. ❤️

I'd been complaining about missing autumn in Aspen. I wanted the colors, cold mountain air, and a little snow.

He remembered.

I leaned over and kissed his cheek.

Jenny was still trying to understand how her boss had arranged an entire mountain getaway without telling her.

"I'm supposed to organize your life!"

"You're doing great."

"EDGAR!"

The cabin was beautiful. Huge windows, a stone fireplace, a deck overlooking the mountains, and golden aspens right outside.

Mia practically ran from the car.

Jack followed her.

Jenny started organizing the bedrooms while I went outside.

Edgar joined me a minute later.

"Well?"

I looked at him.

"You remembered."

"Of course."

He put his arm around me, and we stood there watching the afternoon sunlight catch the mountains.

I kissed his cheek again.

Yes, twice in one afternoon.

He deserved both. 💋 I was a good girl Spencer.

We changed and went into Breckenridge for dinner. The town was gorgeous, and Jenny spent most of the meal informing Edgar about the new policies she intended to implement.

Surprise vacations now require executive approval.

Edgar said he'd consider it.

Jenny said consideration wasn't compliance.

I volunteered to chair the disciplinary committee.

Jack offered to sell tickets.

Mia wanted to know whether there would be prizes.

We are a very mature group of adults. 😂

After dinner, we found some music and went dancing.

Jenny and I attracted attention from two gentlemen who were considerably more confident than interesting.

One asked if I had a boyfriend.

I glanced toward Edgar.

"That's a complicated question."

Jenny nearly choked on her drink.

A little later, she informed Edgar that his assistant required protection from persistent admirers.

"Is that in your job description?"

"I can add it."

Then she took his hand and pulled him toward the music.

I followed.

I love dancing with Edgar. He knows my movements, I know his, and neither of us needs to think about it.

Jenny was laughing beside us, and Mia had her arms around Jack's neck.

I missed Spencer.

She would have loved seeing everyone together, especially Jenny discovering how much teasing Edgar will tolerate.

Quite a lot, as it turns out.

We returned to the cabin and finished the evening in the hot tub. Cold mountain air, steam rising around us, stars overhead.

Then Jack announced he was ordering DoorDash.

"Jack, we already ate."

"Groceries."

Groceries?

At nine o'clock?

Mia grabbed his phone.

Forty-five minutes later, they were STILL shopping.

Jenny leaned over to inspect their cart.

"Gummy worms, waffles, pickles, whipped cream, cereal... What are you two doing?"

"Getting snacks," Jack said.

Mia insisted every item was necessary.

Edgar asked how much they'd spent.

"Around hundred bucks."

"On groceries?"

"Yep."

"That you don't need?"

"We might."

Delivery estimate: 10 PM to midnight.

Jenny stared at them.

"You're having groceries delivered to a mountain cabin at midnight?"

Mia grinned. "Isn't that amazing?"

I looked at Edgar. He looked at Jenny.

We were going to bed.

Last I saw, Jack and Mia were debating whether they'd ordered enough ice cream.

---

And now it’s morning, and I’m back on the deck with my coffee.

I have no idea when their groceries arrived. I'm a little afraid to check the kitchen.

Yesterday was fun. Watching Edgar with his employees, Jenny finding her confidence, Mia and Jack enjoying each other.

But this morning, I keep looking at these aspens.

He remembered.

I know he'll think nothing of it. He had an idea, made a few arrangements, and brought us here.

I wish he could see himself through my eyes occasionally.

We have Mass this morning, and I still need to find a nearby Catholic church. Then I want to walk through these aspens before the remaining leaves disappear.

First, I need to wake everyone.

Although I'm giving Mia and Jack another hour.

They may still be eating "waffles"

Happy Sunday, everyone! ❤️

- Maci 💋

text:
Good morning, you beautiful souls!

Some mornings begin after the victory.

Others begin after the disappointment.

After the prayer seemed unanswered. After the opportunity disappeared. After the relationship became strained. After you gave everything you had and still watched the outcome go in a direction you never wanted.

Those are the mornings that test what your faith is truly built upon.

It is easy to praise God when the door opens, the plan works, and life rewards your effort. It takes a deeper faith to wake up after the loss, sit honestly with the pain, and still believe God has not abandoned your story.

Disappointment does not mean you lacked faith.

Feeling hurt does not make you ungrateful.

Needing rest does not mean you have surrendered.

Jesus understood exhaustion. In Mark 6:31, He told His disciples, “Come with me by yourselves to a quiet place and get some rest.”

He did not shame them for becoming tired. He recognized that people who continuously give, serve, work, and carry responsibility eventually need restoration.

But rest and avoidance are not the same thing.

Rest prepares you to return stronger.

Avoidance keeps you hiding from what needs to change.

Use this Sunday to become quiet enough to recognize the difference.

Ask God to show you what belongs to grief, what belongs to accountability, and what you are carrying that was never yours to control.

If you made a mistake, own it.

If your behavior hurt somebody, repair what you can.

If the outcome was beyond your control, stop punishing yourself for not being powerful enough to change it.

If something ended, take the lesson without allowing bitterness to follow you into every new beginning.

God can redeem a disappointing chapter without pretending the chapter never hurt.

Romans 8:28 does not say everything that happens is good. It tells us that God can work through all things for the good of those who love Him and are called according to His purpose.

That means the failure can teach you.

The rejection can redirect you.

The waiting can strengthen you.

The heartbreak can soften you rather than harden you.

The season that nearly broke you can eventually become the story that helps somebody else remain alive, faithful, and hopeful.

But growth requires your participation.

God can show you the lesson, but you must be humble enough to receive it. He can offer forgiveness, but you must stop returning to the behavior. He can provide strength, but you must eventually stand up and use it.

So breathe today.

Worship without performing.

Rest without feeling guilty.

Tell God the truth about what hurts.

Then ask the harder question: “What are You trying to grow inside me through this?”

You do not have to understand the entire plan before trusting the One who sees it.

Yesterday may have disappointed you, but this morning still arrived carrying mercy.

Your story is not over because one chapter ended painfully.

What lesson can you take from this week without carrying its pain into the week ahead?

I love you. I’m proud of you. I believe in you.

Built from darkness. Driven by light.

text:
Fiona Lali And The Revolutionary Left's Dangerous Romance With Ruthlessness

In July 2025, Fiona Lali offered a revealing glimpse of the politics she wanted Britain's new Left-wing party to embrace. She called for an end to "kind" politics and demanded a ruthless, revolutionary programme built around class struggle. Her justification was that the world itself was unkind. Apparently, the answer to a harsh world is to make politics harsher still.

Lali is no passing protester carried away by an afternoon's excitement. She stood for Parliament in 2024 as a revolutionary communist, became a prominent figure in the Revolutionary Communist Party and published a pamphlet explaining why people should embrace communism. Her political ambitions have been stated openly. She wants capitalism overthrown and a new economic and political order established in its place.

The question is what ruthlessness means when it becomes a political principle. Ruthless towards whom? Political opponents? Businesses? Property owners? Institutions that resist the revolution? And who decides when the revolution has achieved enough to permit disagreement again?

The twentieth century provides ample reason to ask. Lenin's Bolsheviks promised liberation from exploitation and delivered one-party rule, political repression and the machinery of state terror. Mao's revolution promised a new society and produced catastrophic famine, persecution and the destruction of cultural inheritance. Both movements justified extraordinary coercion by appealing to a supposedly greater historical good.

That history does not establish that Lali advocates their crimes. But anyone invoking revolutionary communism while demanding ruthlessness should be prepared to explain which lessons have been learned and which safeguards would prevent another concentration of unchecked power.

There is another contradiction. The revolutionary Left presents itself as the defender of ordinary people against powerful institutions, yet its political language increasingly treats compromise as weakness and ideological certainty as virtue. Democracy depends upon precisely those habits that revolutionary absolutism struggles to accommodate: restraint, pluralism, peaceful disagreement and acceptance that opponents have legitimate rights.

Gaza has become an important rallying point for this movement. Lali's own political literature links opposition to Israel and Western foreign policy with the struggle against capitalism. The revolutionary banners seen at London's Palestine demonstrations reflect that wider agenda. Genuine concern for Palestinian civilians can coexist with an entirely different political project pursued by some of those marching alongside them.

There is also an uncomfortable ideological overlap between sections of the revolutionary Left and Islamist movements. Their ultimate visions of society are profoundly different. One seeks a Marxist transformation, while the other seeks political arrangements rooted in religious authority. Yet hostility towards Israel, Western influence and existing institutions can create temporary common causes. Those connections deserve examination without assuming that every shared demonstration proves an organised alliance.

Britain's universities provide another arena for these ideas. Revolutionary communist organisations openly recruit students, establish societies and encourage political mobilisation. They are entitled to argue their case. Equally, students deserve to encounter the historical record of communist governments, including the consequences of revolutionary movements that placed ideological objectives above individual liberty.

Lali's demand for ruthless politics raises a question. What happens to those who refuse her revolution? After all, democracy permits revolutionaries to campaign and protest, but it must also defend itself against those who would suppress dissent in pursuit of their utopia. History has shown us the consequences.

text:
US Sanctions ICC Hours After Former Judge Wins Nobel Peace Prize, Straining Ties With Europe
WASHINGTON: The Trump administration on Friday imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC), hours after a former judge of the court won the Nobel Peace Prize. The move risks deepening diplomatic tensions between Washington and its European allies.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Trump will never allow the court to prosecute Americans. He said the US would bar dealings with what he called a "rogue" court, cut off its resources and cripple its ability to operate. Unlike earlier sanctions on prosecutors and judges, the new measures could also penalize companies that provide services to the court. The Treasury Department set a six-month grace period and exempted telecommunications, software, pension payments and transactions involving detainees. Rubio said the measures could be adjusted if US demands are not met.
The ICC condemned the step as an attack on the rule of law and urged its 125 member states to act, saying the court "cannot stand alone." Deputy Prosecutor Nazhat Shameem Khan told Reuters its work on all situations, investigations and cases would continue. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the six months offer room for dialogue, adding that the EU has alternative measures to keep the court's key work going. Belgium's foreign minister called on EU states to adopt a blocking statute to counter the sanctions' effects.
Washington has criticized the court over arrest warrants for Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and its Afghanistan probe into US troops' conduct. The court says the Afghanistan case is no longer a priority. The ICC has issued warrants for more than 70 people, including Vladimir Putin and Omar al-Bashir.

text:
Bayard Rustin and Walter Naegle the gay couple who had to use adoption to protect their love.

in 1982, a gay civil rights legend adopted his own boyfriend because the law wouldn't let them get married. 

bayard rustin helped organize the historic 1963 march on washington, fighting for equality while facing discrimination for being gay.

then he fell in love with walter naegle, a man decades younger than him. they built a life together, but there was one problem: the law didn't recognize them as a family.

so rustin adopted walter as his legal son, not because they saw each other as father and son, but because adoption offered a way to secure legal protections their relationship couldn't otherwise receive.

imagine loving someone so deeply that the only legal way to protect your relationship is to become their parent on paper.

they remained partners until rustin's death in 1987.

they were lovers in real life, but the law forced them to become father and son on paper.

Azov and its defenders reject the neo-Nazi label for the unit as a whole, emphasize the “National Idea” explanation, and note that the symbols predate or differ slightly from strict SS versions. Russian state media has heavily amplified the issue as part of its “denazification” narrative for the invasion. Similar far-right symbolism and neo-Nazi groups have also appeared on the Russian side (e.g., Rusich).In short: the primary official-adjacent symbols that draw the Nazi comparisons are the Wolfsangel-like National Idea emblem and (especially early on) the Black Sun. The Totenkopf and other classic Nazi imagery appear mainly at the individual or subunit level rather than as the unit’s formal badge. The visual and historical overlaps are real and documented, even as the unit and its supporters offer alternative interpretations and the broader Ukrainian military is not defined by them.The Azov Battalion (later Regiment/Brigade, now part of the National Guard and the 1st Azov Corps) has used several symbols that closely resemble or match those associated with Nazi Germany and neo-Nazi groups. The main ones tied to the unit or its members are the Wolfsangel-like “National Idea” emblem, the Black Sun (Sonnenrad), and (among individuals or subunits) the Totenkopf (death’s head).en.wikipedia.org +1Wolfsangel / “National Idea” (Ідея Нації)Azov’s core emblem is a stylized monogram of the Ukrainian letters “I” and “N” (often rendered as ꑭ or similar), called the “National Idea” or “Idea of the Nation.” Visually, it is a close match or mirrored variation of the Wolfsangel (wolf’s hook), a medieval heraldic symbol later used by several Waffen-SS units, most notably the 2nd SS Panzer Division “Das Reich.”The symbol came from the Social-National Party of Ukraine and was used by the Patriot of Ukraine and Social-National Assembly—far-right groups whose members formed the core of Azov in 2014 under founder Andriy Biletsky.
Azov has consistently stated that it represents “united nation” or “national idea,” not the SS symbol.

Early versions featured it prominently; the Black Sun was later dropped from the official logo (around 2015), and designs evolved (sometimes more angular or “attacking”). Related units (including elements of the 3rd Assault Brigade) continue using versions of it. It remains associated with Azov and Ukrainian far-right nationalism more https://t.co/gwlURviZgf +1Black Sun (Sonnenrad / Schwarze Sonne)The founding Azov emblem placed the National Idea symbol over a Black Sun (a sun wheel of 12 radial Sig runes). This design is the specific version created or popularized in the SS context—most famously inlaid in the floor of Wewelsburg Castle, Heinrich Himmler’s SS ideological center. Post-war, it became a common neo-Nazi, occult, and white-nationalist symbol (used as a less overt alternative to the swastika).Azov removed it from the official unit logo, but it has continued to appear on flags, patches, personal tattoos, and among related personnel or https://t.co/QasT60nHrG +1Totenkopf (Death’s Head)This is not the official unit emblem of Azov itself, but skull-and-crossbones imagery matching or closely resembling the SS Totenkopf (used by SS units and especially the Totenkopfverbände concentration-camp guard formations) has been documented on uniforms, patches, and tattoos of some Azov-linked or other Ukrainian soldiers. Individual fighters and certain subunits have used it. Note that death’s-head symbols have older military uses (e.g., Prussian hussars), but the specific SS version carries the Nazi https://t.co/laG35SClEQ +1Other Associated SymbolsMembers and related personnel have also been photographed with or tattooed with swastikas, SS Sig runes, “88” (Heil Hitler), “1488,” and other runic or neo-pagan symbols common in far-right circles. These are generally personal rather than official unit insignia. Early reporting (including by German media) showed such imagery on helmets and gear in 2014.Context and DisputesAzov was founded in 2014 as a volunteer battalion drawing heavily from the ultranationalist/far-right Patriot of Ukraine and Social-National Assembly. Founder Andriy Biletsky (sometimes called the “White Leader”) made explicit racial statements, including the widely reported claim that Ukraine’s historical mission was to “lead the white races of the world in a final crusade… against Semite-led Untermenschen.” A 2015 unit spokesperson estimated that 10–20% of recruits at the time were Nazis. The unit was later integrated into the National Guard; some observers describe a degree of depoliticization or moderation as it professionalized, while others note that far-right symbols, ideology, and personnel links persist in the broader “Azov movement” and successor https://t.co/8IJG3tMtHY +1

The United States is engaged in a confrontation with Iran, while Russia has been reported as providing various forms of support to Tehran. Against that backdrop, the decision to allow increased Russian diesel exports, reportedly aimed at lowering fuel costs, raises important strategic questions.

In a recent announcement, President Trump outlined an arrangement that would permit Russia to supply diesel to U.S. and international markets, along with temporary sanctions relief. At the same time, reports have indicated that Russia has offered assistance to Iran during the ongoing conflict.

Critics argue that this creates an apparent policy inconsistency. On one hand, Washington is taking a hard line against Iran; on the other, it is easing economic restrictions on a country accused of backing Tehran.

There is no direct evidence that revenues from the proposed fuel arrangement have funded actions against U.S. forces. Nevertheless, the public is entitled to understand how policymakers evaluated the potential geopolitical risks against the anticipated economic benefits.

Reducing energy costs is a legitimate objective. However, any effort to lower fuel prices should be examined carefully to ensure it does not unintentionally strengthen governments whose interests may conflict with those of the United States.

Several questions remain unanswered. What conditions and protections are built into the agreement? What commitments, if any, were secured from Moscow? And to what extent will consumers actually benefit from lower fuel prices?

Rather than accepting the deal at face value, lawmakers and the public should closely scrutinize its long-term economic and strategic implications.

The central issue is whether this represents a carefully calculated diplomatic move or an expensive policy choice that could generate unintended consequences in the future.

text:
How Israel Views Gaza, One Year after the Ceasefire - Brig.-Gen. (ret.) Michael Herzog
The Trump plan for Gaza, launched last year, explicitly laid out Israel's goals: releasing all the hostages (which was implemented), disarming Hamas, removing it from power, and ensuring that Gaza could no longer be used as a platform for threatening Israel.
    The plan offered a mostly political path to realizing these elusive goals, without enforcement on the ground. Yet Israel does not believe this approach will work with a violent Islamist actor like Hamas. It has therefore kept constant physical pressure on Hamas, conditioning any reconstruction on the group's disarmament.
    Israel has continuously targeted senior terrorists and military infrastructure in the area under Hamas control, with quiet American consent, disrupting Hamas efforts to reassert governance and recover some of its military capabilities.
    For Israel, disarming Hamas and other terrorist organizations in Gaza is the most important task. Israel insists that demilitarization be inclusive, comprehensive, verifiable, and permanent. Israel insists that until a full, verifiable disarmament process is completed, the IDF will conduct no further redeployments.
    Despite the current environment of skepticism, Hamas has been significantly weakened militarily, financially, and politically. According to recent polls, Palestinian public support for the group and the "armed struggle" it represents has declined significantly.
 The writer, a fellow of the Washington Institute, is a former Israeli ambassador to the U.S. and former chief of staff to Israel's minister of defense.  (Washington Institute for Near East Policy)

When *March and March* leads poor mothers from Diepsloot, Hillbrow, and Delft to march against illegal migration - against overcrowded clinics where South Africans are told to go home, against spaza shops selling poisoned food to our children, against jobs being undercut by R30 a day - you call them *"a threat to democracy."*

That is not journalism. That is apartheid bias in a digital suit.

*1. What March and March is doing is DEMOCRACY.*

Section 17 of the Constitution: _Everyone has the right to assemble, to demonstrate, to picket._

Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma did not go to a foreign government. She went to the streets of her own country. She raised an issue that is REAL.

Go to Pretoria, to Marabastad. Go to Durban, to Point Road. Go to Cape Town, to Bellville. Poor South Africans live with illegal migration daily. Not the way you live in Gardens or Sandton with private security and Discovery Health. They share one RDP with 8 undocumented tenants. Their children sit 65 in a classroom. Their clinics run out of ARVs.

They have the right to protest that. You may not like the slogan, you may call it xenophobia, but it is not a threat to democracy. It IS democracy - messy, angry, poor people shouting.

*2. What AfriForum is doing IS a threat to democracy, and you never write it.*

Define threat to democracy:

- Lobbying a foreign power to impose economic sanctions on your own country to force your parliament to change its laws? That is treason in America. In South Africa, News24 calls it "lobbying."
- In February 2025, AfriForum and Solidarity went to the White House and presented a dossier saying "white genocide." Result: Trump cut aid, offered refugee status to Whites only, threatened trade.
- That cut directly threatens democracy: 5.5 million HIV patients dependent on US-funded programs. Jobs in auto and agriculture dependent on AGOA. When you cut that because Kallie Kriel doesn't like the Expropriation Act, you are holding the entire country hostage.

Did News24 write an editorial: _"AfriForum is a threat to democracy. It must be stopped"_? No.

Did News24 write it when AfriForum asked for US intervention against our Constitutional Court? No. Why?

*3. Because News24 has two definitions of democracy:*

- *AfriKan protest = threat.* Whether it's EFF with "Kill the Boer", or March and March with "Put South Africans First", or Fees Must Fall - it's always "violent, divisive, threat to democracy."

- *White lobby = democracy.* Whether it's AfriForum begging for sanctions, or Sakeliga suing transformation, or DA going to Washington to say "don't punish us, punish ANC" - it's always "civil society, constitutional rights."

That is the white supremacy you have institutionalized.

Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma is not funded by Washington. She does not have a lobbyist in DC. She does not meet with John Steenhuisen's bosses at the Cato Institute.

AfriForum does.

If you want to stop a threat to democracy, stop the people who have the power to actually kill democracy - those with foreign bank accounts, with 77% of farmland, with access to the Oval Office.

March and March has no power to impose sanctions. They only have their feet.

AfriForum has the power to make America punish South Africa. And they used it.

*News24, you are not the referee of democracy.*

You are owned by Naspers - a company that thrived under Apartheid censorship, that printed racial propaganda for 70 years. You never editorialized that Naspers was a threat to democracy. Today you want to teach poor Black women about democracy?

We see you.

text:
Sanctuary States Don’t Protect Immigrants. They Use Them.

Sanctuary states like to cloak themselves in the language of empathy. 

They tell voters they are standing up for vulnerable people, resisting cruelty, and choosing compassion over enforcement. 

But strip away the rhetoric and a colder motive emerges.

This isn’t about helping illegal immigrants. It’s about political power.

Under the Constitution, congressional representation and Electoral College votes are based on total population—not citizenship. That means states can increase their power in Washington simply by counting people, even if those people have no legal status, no vote, and no real path to stability. 

The incentive is obvious: maximize population, minimize responsibility.

The result is a permanent underclass. Millions of people are allowed to remain in legal limbo—working, paying taxes, raising children, but never fully integrating—because their presence benefits the political class more than their freedom ever would.

This logic is not novel. It is disturbingly familiar.

At the Constitutional Convention, slave states fought aggressively to count enslaved people toward representation, despite denying them every civil and political right. The justification was nakedly transactional: bodies translated into power. The infamous Three-Fifths Compromise wasn’t born of confusion or moral blindness; it was a deliberate strategy to inflate influence while preserving control.

Today’s sanctuary policies follow the same structural logic. People are counted, not represented. 

Valued for their numbers, not their dignity. 

Useful precisely because they cannot vote, cannot leave easily, and cannot demand better from the politicians who claim to defend them.

If this were truly about compassion, the policy focus would be legalization, work authorization, geographic mobility, and integration. 

Instead, we get symbolic defiance, selective enforcement, and endless limbo—conditions that keep labor cheap, communities dependent, and political power safely concentrated at the top.

Calling this empathy is a moral inversion.

Empathy seeks to elevate people into full participants in civic life. 

What sanctuary states offer instead is containment: just enough protection to keep people here, never enough justice to let them fully belong.

That is not solidarity. It is demographic gerrymandering.

And tens of millions of human beings are the pawns.

When bodies matter more than freedom, the system isn’t broken. It’s working exactly as designed.

Yes, Cancel the Long End and Start YCC. 

Let’s give some context and be explicit.

Cancel the long-end auctions and bring on targeted yield-curve control. Buy time, focus the strategy, rebuild America.

Reagan’s rule was “Trust, but verify.” 

But, the  bond vigilantes have skipped the first half. They don’t trust the Fed, Bessent, Trump or Washington. In a period of historic change, they demand concrete evidence. A rational response, buy time by cancelling auction on the long end and bring back YCC. 

This is about credibility, not simply inflation. The confrontation echoes the Hillarycare era, when bond vigilantes challenged Clinton’s ambitions and ten-year Treasury yields climbed above 8%.

Court action disrupted tariff collections and forced refunds, damaging revenue that could help narrow the deficit. Replacement duties should recover part of the loss. 

The vigilantes don’t care about the explanation. They want receipts.
Cancel the auctions until they are in hand!

Supply-side economics takes time. Full expensing rewards qualifying investment before its productivity dividend arrives. AI offers a generational opportunity. 

The GENIUS Act could strengthen dollar-based finance and Treasury demand. Foundations are forming; results must follow.

Warsh’s Fed needs a makeover. Trimmed-mean PCE near 2.2% is concrete evidence against a broad inflationary cascade, and below the 2.7% reading available when Powell cut rates by 50 basis points in September 2024. 

Recall October 2018: weeks before the midterms, amid the escalating China trade conflict, Powell declared rates “a long way from neutral” and entertained going beyond it. 

By late November, they were “just below” neutral; the following year brought three cuts. Warsh’s Fed is doing the same political maneuver. 

That is a record of miscalculation and inconsistent communication. Warsh must stop repeating it. Let the data discipline the theory, rather than treating economic strength as an automatic invitation to tighten.

Bessent should temporarily suspend new 20- and 30-year auctions, accepting greater refinancing risk. Warsh and Bessent need to revisit the possibility of yield-curve control, aligning Treasury’s financing strategy with an independently determined Fed framework. 

Targeted yield caps should address market dysfunction, not subsidize deficits regardless of inflation. Buying time must not become an excuse to abandon fiscal discipline.

America First requires priorities. No more wars. End the Iran conflict. Rebuild America’s productive economy. Give the Bond Vigilantes the receipts. 

America grew out of debt after World War II. Gross federal debt fell from roughly 125% of GDP to the mid 30% in 1975. Nominal growth and fiscal restraint worked together
.
The vigilantes trade by the minute; productive investment takes years.
Make 2027 the proof: recovering revenue, expanding capacity, peace and borrowing growing slower than output.

Buy time, not excuses. Outgrow the debt. Rebuild America.

text: Here we are again... We would be getting everything ready to go and Gary would be yelling at me about things because he knew that I knew it was meant for everyone and I didn't care 😏. I would arrive to Alred Marina and always be amazed at all the hard work that had been done leading up to that Sunday, since I was one of the few sailors not local. The entire boat had to be transformed to accommodate up to 25 people with extra bunk bed cots set up extra refrigerators and freezers for all the food for the trip and supplies for the tailgate once we arrived. Sunday families would join us for the start of the trip and be dropped off at Goose Pond. Then we would start the trek and anchor for the night in the far end of Lake Guntersville. This is also where the first of the technical issues would occur when the boat only moves that far every 2 years. Generator issues, HVAC, engine cooling intakes, the very finicky clearing throat.. waste system. But that was always part of it and Gary would always be all over it and wouldn't stop until a solution or stop gap until the solution was found. It really was two trips in one. The amazing trip up the river seeing all the fall foliage and going through each lock and dam. Stopping each night at specific locations strategically chosen by Gary for what it offered the crew and each night different. Then the second part of the tailgating in the Vol Navy. We would arrive Thursday afternoon and we're always welcomed with open arms and hospitality. While we were majority Bama fans we always had at least a couple of UT fans on the trip with us. 3 of the most amazing weeks of my life and met so many amazing people and none of it happens without Gary. The irony is we really didn't spend a lot of time together on the trips but we really didn't need to. He loved seeing me experiencing everything and meeting all his friends that I didn't know since we moved away from Huntsville, and I loved seeing him in his element, orchestrating everything and making sure everyone had the time of their lives. I still have people being the trips up to me, people who saw us on TV or randomly stopped by and tailgated and some of you here who went to one of the games and tailgated with us. It was all because of him. The other two owners of the boat were huge too of course but it was Gary who had been dreaming of this since we were in middle school and he made it happen. I miss him so much every day but especially this week but I am also so grateful we had those 3 trips together (there were 4 total but I missed the first due to a previous commitment before the trip was confirmed, and I never heard the end of it). RIP Gary. Fuck cancer. Roll Tide. Go Big Orange... And get your colonoscopies and don't ignore symptoms. Make your doc schedule your first if you haven't had one yet.

text:
WYTHEVILLE, Virginia — Most people meet this town zooming past it at 70 miles an hour.
Interstate 77 comes up out of North Carolina Interstate 81 runs down the Great Valley toward Bristol. They cross here, share a few miles of pavement, and then split again. Truckers stop for diesel. Families stop for a bathroom. Then they are gone.
They miss the better road.
U.S. 11 runs right through downtown as Main Street. In this part of Virginia it is also called the Lee Highway. 
Before that it was the Great Road, the wagon road that carried settlers south out of Pennsylvania and Maryland and down the valley toward Cumberland Gap. Virginia now signs the corridor as the Wilderness Road: Virginia’s Heritage Migration Route About 10 miles east, at Fort Chiswell, long hunters set out in 1761 for the country beyond the mountains.
On March 10, 1775, Daniel Boone and some 30 axmen set out from the Long Island of the Holston near present-day Kingsport, Tennessee, to cut a path through Cumberland Gap into Kentucky. The crown had banned settlement beyond the mountains They went anyway. Hundreds of thousands of settlers followed, and many of them came down this valley to get there.
That was 250 years ago. Virginia and Kentucky spent last year marking the anniversary with reenactors, relay hikes, and a ceremonial ax carried from Kingsport to Fort Boonesborough.
This year the country marks its own 250th.
